# CLAUDE.md

This file captures only what cannot be inferred from the codebase itself.

## Rules for editing this file

Both developers and AI agents are expected to add entries as they encounter surprises.

- **Add an entry** when you encounter something unexpected: a build quirk, a non-obvious constraint, a dependency gotcha, or any behavior that would surprise the next agent or developer.
- **Add an entry** when a developer flags an anti-pattern produced by AI — describe the anti-pattern and the preferred alternative.
- **Do not** add codebase overviews, directory listings, or anything discoverable by reading the source.
- Keep entries concise: one line per lesson, grouped under a heading if a theme emerges.
- **Durable-invariant test** before adding a gotcha: "Would a future agent rediscover this in under 60 seconds via Grep + reading source?" If yes, it belongs in the git commit message, not here. Every entry costs tokens on every session — the bar for inclusion is **future agents will break things if they don't know this**. Per-fix narratives (test name, specific code path, fix story) go in PLAN-PHASE-4.md session notes instead.

## Known gotchas

- **Do NOT poll for a Gradle run with a `while kill -0 $(pgrep -f "GradleWrapperMain.*jvmTest") ...; do sleep N; done` wait-loop — it never exits.** `pgrep -f` matches against the FULL command line, and the wait-loop's OWN command line literally contains the string `GradleWrapperMain.*jvmTest` (inside the pgrep pattern), so it matches ITSELF → `kill -0 <self-pid>` always succeeds → the loop sleeps forever, orphaned (harmless/idle, but never terminates and clutters the process list; clean up with `kill <pids>`). There is no need to poll at all: launch the suite with the Bash tool's `run_in_background: true` and react to the `<task-notification>` that fires when it completes (the harness re-invokes you). If you must poll for something, pick a pattern that cannot match the poller itself (e.g. a marker file's existence). Two long-lived JVMs (the Gradle daemon + `KotlinCompileDaemon`, ~hours uptime) are NORMAL idle build daemons — leave them; they speed up builds and auto-shut-down after their idle timeout.
- `project.exec {}` is not available in Gradle 9 Kotlin DSL task `doLast` blocks — use `ProcessBuilder` directly instead.
- TypeScript compiler tests are **generated** by `./gradlew generateTypeScriptTests` into `build/generated/typescript-tests/`; this task requires the TypeScript repo to be cloned first (done automatically via `cloneTypeScriptRepo` dependency). Never edit generated files manually.
- **Deprecated features skipped in JS emit tests**: Parameterized JS emit tests for `target=ES5`/`ES3` and `module=AMD`/`System`/`UMD` are not generated (deprecated in TypeScript 6.0, removed in 7.0/tsgo). Error baseline tests for these combinations ARE still generated since TS5107/TS5108 deprecation diagnostics must still fire. The `effectiveTarget` maps ES3/ES5 → ES2015 so no downlevel transforms are needed.
- **Disabled test category**: `.errors.txt` error baseline tests are commented out in `build.gradle.kts` `generateTypeScriptTests` task — search for `TODO: Re-enable when type checker is implemented`. Re-enabling adds ~9,055 tests (see PLAN.md item 4c).
- Kotlin 2.x disallows `.` in backtick-quoted JVM method names (error: "Name contains illegal characters: .."); sanitize test function names by replacing dots with underscores (e.g. `foo_ts` not `foo.ts`). Some TypeScript test base names contain dots beyond the extension (e.g. `accessors_spec_section-4.5_error-cases`), so the entire `nameWithoutExtension` must have dots replaced, not just the `.ts`/`.js` suffix.

### Checker walker gotchas

- **Any NEW full-tree expression walker MUST handle `BinaryExpression` iteratively (worklist/right-spine), not recursively** — `binderBinaryExpressionStress` is a deeply-nested `a+b+c+…` chain that StackOverflows a naive `walk(left); walk(right)`, and a crash mid-check ABORTS JS emit, so the regression shows up as a JS-EMIT output diff (NOT in the `find_candidates` EXTRA bucket — only the failing-set diff catches it). B98b's `walkThisTypeExpr` learned this the hard way. Reference iterative patterns: `checkArgCountInExprCore`'s BinaryExpression case (right-spine while-loop) and B98b's worklist (`ArrayDeque` frontier).
- **MappedType walkers must remember to walk `typeParameter.constraint`**: A `MappedType` AST node has FOUR meaningful child positions: `typeParameter.constraint` (the constraint of `[K in C]`, e.g. `keyof T`), `nameType` (after `as`), `type` (the value), and the typeParameter NAME (introduced into a child scope). Tree-walking visitors must hit all four. Crucially the constraint must be walked in the OUTER `scope` (not the mapped child scope) — the TP being introduced is NOT in scope inside its own constraint. Reference patterns: `collectTypeReferenceNames` (Checker.kt:3890) and `checkUnresolvedInType` (Checker.kt:13931) both walk the constraint correctly. Symptom of forgetting: TS2304 / TS2503 / TS6133 for a name only-used inside the constraint silently never fires.

### Scanner/Parser gotchas

- **A `#`-private class-member name node KEEPS the leading `#` in its `.text`, and `.pos` points AT the `#` (B98.r144)**: despite `parsePropertyName`'s `Hash -> { nextToken(); parseIdentifierName() }` branch SUGGESTING the `#` is consumed/stripped, the scanner emits `#context` as a single token, so the resulting `Identifier` has `.text == "#context"` and `.pos` at the `#`. To detect a private member, test `name.text.startsWith("#")` — do NOT check `source[name.pos - 1] == '#'` (that lands on the char before `#`, e.g. whitespace, and silently matches nothing). This bit the first cut of `checkExportedAnonClassExprPrivateMembers` (TS4094).
- **Multi-base heritage with a GENERIC base before a comma is MISPARSED (B93/round-79 finding, NOT yet fixed)**: `interface C extends A<string>, A<number> { }` (or `class C implements A<X>, B<Y>`) — the FIRST base (the one followed by `,`) is parsed as a synthetic `ParenthesizedExpression` (an instantiation-expression `A<string>`) instead of an `ExpressionWithTypeArguments`, so its `.typeArguments` are LOST (and the type-arg node's `.end` overshoots, doubling the trailing `>` in a source-substring). The LAST base (followed by `{`) parses correctly. Consequence: `checkInterfaceMultiBaseConflicts` (Checker.kt:~59857) sees only ONE resolved base for a same-base-different-args conflict, so TS2320 ("cannot simultaneously extend types 'A<string>' and 'A<number>'") silently never fires (e.g. `multipleBaseInterfaesWithIncompatibleProperties`). Root cause is in the heritage-clause base-type parsing (instantiation-expression disambiguation kicking in when a generic type ref is followed by `,`). Fixing it is in the Parser and is risk-bearing (affects all multi-base `extends`/`implements`); deferred. **Checker-side workaround LANDED for the TS2320 same-base case (B98.r128d, `checkMultiBaseInStatement`)**: rather than depend on the dropped `.typeArguments` (or the `.end`-overshoot-doubled `>`), extract each heritage base's `(name, typeArgs)` UNIFORMLY from SOURCE — find the base name's `<` and bracket-match to its `>`, splitting args by top-level commas. This sidesteps both the misparse and the overshoot, so `interface C extends A<string>, A<number>` (same base `A`, different args) fires TS2320 + the "Named property 'x' of types 'A<string>' and 'A<number>' are not identical" chain. The general multi-base TS2320 conflict path (different base names) still relies on `resolveBaseSym`, which returns null for the misparsed `ParenthesizedExpression` base — so a same-base-different-args conflict needs the source-extraction path, NOT the property loop (which skips it at `distinctBases<2`).
- **JSX-vs-generic-arrow disambiguation in `.tsx` files**: In `parsePrimaryExpression`'s `LessThan` branch, when `isJsxFile`, peek at `<Identifier extends X...>`. If X is an Identifier / type-keyword / open delimiter / `typeof` → generic arrow, fall through to the existing generic-arrow / type-assertion detection. If X is `/`, `>`, or `=` → JSX (boolean attr shorthand `<T extends/>` or attr=value `<T extends={x}/>`). The broader gate `<Identifier extends` (without checking what follows) regresses `parseJsxExtends2_ts`. Tightened gate fixes both `parseJsxExtends2_ts` (JSX) and `declarationEmitRecursiveConditionalAliasPreserved_ts` (generic arrow).


- **`lookAhead` vs `tryScan`**: `lookAhead` ALWAYS restores scanner state. `tryScan` keeps scanner state if callback returns truthy. Use `lookAhead` for probe-and-decide patterns; use `tryScan` for "try to parse, keep results if success."
- **A *parenthesized* function/ctor type is a `ParenthesizedType`, NOT a bare `FunctionType`/`ConstructorType` (B98.r76)**: `parseFunctionOrParenthesizedType` returns a bare `FunctionType` for `() => void` but wraps `(() => void)` in `ParenthesizedType(FunctionType)` (the fallback at Parser.kt:~6823). So any grammar check that needs "is this an UNparenthesized fn/ctor type as a union/intersection member" (TS1385/1386/1387/1388) just tests `member is FunctionType || member is ConstructorType` — the legal parenthesized form is a `ParenthesizedType` and won't match. For the member's diagnostic SPAN matching TS (which includes the leading trivia after the `|`/`&`): `scanner.getPrevTokenEnd()` immediately after `parseOptional(Bar/Ampersand)` = the position right after the `|`/`&` (start, incl. the following space), and `scanner.getPrevTokenEnd()` immediately after parsing the member = the member's TRUE end (avoids the `node.end` overshoot). Mixed `A | B & () => C | () => D` shapes report at multiple nesting depths for free because a function type's RETURN is parsed via the recursive `parseType`. Message article is "a union" but "an intersection".
- **`lookAhead` does NOT restore diagnostics**: The parser's `lookAhead` restores scanner position and the `token` field, but any `reportError`/`parseExpected` failures during the callback permanently add to `diagnostics`. When using `lookAhead` with complex parsing (e.g., `parseComputedPropertyName()`), save `diagnostics.size` before and trim after to discard speculative errors.
- **`reScanGreaterToken`** (splitting `>>` to `>` for nested generics) was implemented but caused 4-test net regression — left disabled in the parser. The implementation in `Scanner.kt` is correct; the issue is likely subtle interaction with `tryScan` nesting. Re-enable cautiously.
- **`getPos()` in Parser** = `scanner.getTokenPos()` (start of current token), **`getEnd()`** = `scanner.getPos()` (end of current token text). After `parseExpected()`, the scanner has ALREADY advanced to the next token — so `getPos()` is the start of the NEXT token.
- **Case clause singleLine detection**: Check `source.substring(caseStartPos, firstStmtStart).contains('\n')` to determine if statements are on the same line as `case:`. Do NOT use `scanner.getPos()` after `parseExpected(Colon)` since the scanner has advanced past the colon into the next token's trivia.
- **TS1007 related info for missing close delimiters**: Use `parseExpectedClosing()` (not `parseExpected`) when closing `)` in statement-level constructs (`if`, `while`, `with`, `do-while`). This provides `!!! related TS1007` pointing back to the opening `(`. DO NOT use this globally (in `parseExpected`) — it causes 59+ FP regressions in error recovery tests because the `openTokenStack` doesn't track delimiter types and pops incorrectly in complex error recovery scenarios. For general `parseExpected(CloseParen/CloseBrace)`, only emit TS1007 at EOF (current behavior).
- **Extending squiggle span to include `;`**: When a parser diagnostic should cover the trailing `;` (e.g. `[]: number;` → entire 14-char span), call `parseSemicolon()` first (consuming `;` if present), then use `scanner.getPrevTokenEnd()` for the span end. `getEnd()` is wrong because it returns the scanner position AFTER the next token is scanned. `scanner.getPrevTokenEnd()` = position right after the last-consumed token's text, before the next token's trivia.

- **`isStartOfType` inside `scanner.lookAhead`**: Parser's cached `token` field is NOT updated inside `scanner.lookAhead`. When checking what token follows, pass `scanner.getToken()` explicitly: `isStartOfType(scanner.getToken())`. Using the parser's `token` field inside lookAhead checks the OLD token (before the lookAhead scan), not the advanced token.
- **JSDoc nullable `?` in type context**: TypeScript's parser handles `?` before/after types as JSDoc nullable syntax (TS17019/TS17020). Our parser adds error recovery in `parseNonUnionType()`: leading `?` consumed before primary type, trailing `?` consumed with lookahead guard (only when NOT followed by a type-start token — prevents eating conditional type `?`). Bare `?` with no following type returns `any`.

- **`TemplateLiteralType` parser is shallow — `templateSpans = emptyList()` always (B65.1)**: `Parser.kt:6629-6641`'s `Backtick`/`NoSubstitutionTemplateLiteral`/`TemplateHead` branch skips over the entire template-literal type via `skipTemplateType()` and stores the raw source slice in `head.rawText`. The `templateSpans` list is ALWAYS empty — even when the template contains `${infer X}` or `${TypeName}` placeholders. Consequence: any checker walker that needs to see the AST structure inside `${...}` (e.g. `collectInferTypeNames` to scope `infer X` declarations into the conditional's trueType) gets nothing useful. **B80.1 mitigation (`infer NAME` only)**: `collectInferTypeNames` calls `extractInferNamesFromRawTemplate(head.rawText, scope)` which string-scans the raw text for `${...infer NAME...}` (whitespace-tolerant) and adds NAME to the scope via `scope.addTypeParam`. This suppresses FP TS2304 for the trueType's use of the inferred name. Other walkers needing `${TypeName}` REFERENCE tracking (unused-name, type-reference graphs) would need the same raw-text pattern — the helper is name-extraction-only. Proper `TemplateLiteralTypeSpan(type: TypeNode)` parsing remains out-of-scope for surgical fixes; what's mitigated is one specific FP class.

### Emitter gotchas

- **Tab preservation in error squiggles**: The error baseline formatter must preserve tab characters from source lines in the squiggle indentation — tabs stay as tabs, other characters become spaces. Don't use `" ".repeat(col)`.
- **Numeric literal property access**: `1.foo` is ambiguous in JS (the `.` is a decimal point). Emit `1..foo` when the numeric literal has no decimal point, exponent, or `0x`/`0b`/`0o` prefix.
- **Yield expression operand parsing**: Use `isStartOfExpression()` check (not `!canParseSemicolon()`) to determine if yield has an operand. `canParseSemicolon()` returns false for `]` and `)` which would cause yield to try parsing them as expressions. TypeScript checks `!hasPrecedingLineBreak() && (asterisk || isStartOfExpression())`.

### Transformer gotchas

- **Orphaned comments (erased declarations)**: Only preserve a leading comment from an erased declaration if there is a blank line (≥2 newlines) between the comment's `end` position and the declaration's `pos`. Adjacent comments are part of the declaration and are dropped.
- **CommonJS transform ordering**: Applied AFTER all other transforms. `transformToCommonJS` receives already-transformed statements. The `isModuleFile` check uses the ORIGINAL source file statements.
- **`transformToCommonJS` is CJS-only**: returns early for ESM/AMD/UMD/System outputs. Any post-process placed inside it (e.g., decorator-metadata safety wraps) won't fire for those module formats. For across-module-format post-processing, add the code to `transformPhase3`'s tail (after the AMD/UMD/System branches return, just before the final `return sourceFile.copy(statements = ...)`). Symptom of getting this wrong: code compiles clean, test still fails with the same diff, debug println never prints.
- **Constructor prologue ordering**: When inserting parameter-property initializers into an existing constructor body (no `super()` call), insert AFTER prologue directives (`"use strict"`, `"ngInject"`), not at index 0.
- **Type assertion parens**: `(<T>expr)` — the Transformer (not Emitter) must drop them. Fix belongs in Transformer because `TypeAssertionExpression` is already stripped before Emitter sees it.
- **`new (<T>call())` semantics**: `new (A())` ≠ `new A()` — after stripping the type assertion, if the constructor expr becomes a `CallExpression`, it must be re-wrapped in `ParenthesizedExpression`.
- **Static-class-field async arrow defensive capture**: For `class C { static field = async (...) => ... }` under target<ES2022, TypeScript pre-emits `var _a; _a = C;` even when the async arrow body has no `this` reference. The `__awaiter` template is conceptually `this`-binding for static-field-initialized async arrows even when the actual `__awaiter` call passes `void 0`. `staticPropsWithThis` filter in `Transformer.kt` matches this shape via `prop.initializer is ArrowFunction && ModifierFlag.Async in modifiers`. Skip the gate at your peril — removing it regresses `asyncArrowInClassES5_ts`.
- **Chained safety wrap for cross-file `declare namespace` in `design:paramtypes`**: For `f(@deco arg: A.B.C.D.E): void` where `A` is `declare namespace A { ... }` in another file (no value exports), the metadata emit must defensively wrap: `typeof (_d = typeof A !== "undefined" && (_a = A.B) !== void 0 && (_b = _a.C) !== void 0 && (_c = _b.D) !== void 0 && _c.E) === "function" ? _d : Object`. `wrapDeepQualifiedNameForMetadata` in `Transformer.kt` does this. Gate is `checker.isTypeOnlyGlobalName(baseName)` — when the root is a runtime value (e.g. `declare namespace A { export var foo }`), fall through to raw `qualifiedNameToPropertyAccess`. Temp vars `_a, _b, ..., _<max>` are hoisted at file top via `maxDeepMetadataTempCount` field tracked across the file's serialization passes.
- **Async-arrow destructuring-param capture (target<ES2017)**: When `async (...) => ...` has any `ObjectBindingPattern` / `ArrayBindingPattern` parameter, TypeScript rewrites the OUTER arrow's params to simple-identifier proxies and moves the original parameters (with destructuring) into the inner `function*` generator inside `__awaiter`. Proxies pass values via `__awaiter`'s 2nd arg (args array). Identifier params get `<name>_<i+1>`; binding patterns get fresh `_a`/`_b`/... Example: `async (dispatch, { foo }) => ...` → `(dispatch_1, _a) => __awaiter(void 0, [dispatch_1, _a], void 0, function* (dispatch, { foo }) { ... })`. Gate in `Transformer.kt`'s async-arrow path: `hasBindingPattern && !hasRestParam`. Pure-Identifier async arrows keep the existing simpler emit.
- **Optional-call downlevel needs `.call(receiver, ...)` for method/index access (target<ES2020)**: For `obj.method?.(args)` or `obj[key]?.(args)`, the downleveled form must use `_a.call(obj, ...args)` rather than `_a(args)` so the `this` binding is preserved (matches the runtime semantics of `?.()`). Gate in `Transformer.kt`'s CallExpression `questionDotToken` branch: when LHS is PropertyAccess/ElementAccess with simple-Identifier receiver, emit `.call(receiver, ...args)`; otherwise fall through to the plain `_a(args)` form.
- **Non-async arrow expression-body must scope its own hoists**: For `() => obj?.foo` (any arrow whose body is an expression containing temp-var-needing transforms), push a `hoistedVarScopes` entry around body transformation. If any temps were allocated, convert the expression body to `{ var <temps>; return <body>; }`. Without this, optional-chain temp vars hoist to the outer file scope, mismatching TypeScript's emit shape. Async arrows skip this push because `__awaiter` provides its own wrapper.
- **`__decorate` emission for accessor pairs (B70.16)**: TypeScript emits ONE `__decorate` call per accessor PAIR, not per accessor. The leading accessor (in source order) owns the emission; its `__decorate` args include the leading accessor's own decorators AND the paired accessor's `__param(idx, dec)` entries for parameter decorators. In `generateMemberDecorateStatements`: GetAccessor branch pulls a paired SetAccessor's parameter decorators when the setter appears LATER in source. SetAccessor branch `continue`s when paired with a GetAccessor that appears EARLIER. Setter-only or setter-first cases still emit the setter's own `__decorate` with its parameter decorators (the SetAccessor `paramDecorators` field MUST be populated from `member.parameters` in that case — hardcoding it to empty loses the param decorators).
- **`__decorate` emission ordering: non-static before static**: TypeScript emits all instance-side member `__decorate` calls BEFORE all static-side ones (within each group, source order is preserved). In `generateMemberDecorateStatements`, iterate `members.filter { !static } + members.filter { static }` instead of plain `members` to match. Symptom of getting this wrong: a static field's `__decorate` block appears mid-instance-block in the output diff.

- **TS18046 ('X is of type unknown') for a DEREFERENCED `unknown`-typed SIMPLE-identifier catch variable is a CONSERVATIVE straight-line walker, NOT flow-narrowing (B142, `checkUnknownCatchVarUsage`)**: sibling of B139's destructuring check (same `unknown` gate: explicit `: unknown`, else effective `useUnknownInCatchVariables`). It scans ONLY the straight-line LEADING catch-body statements and STOPS at the first control-flow statement (if/while/for/switch/try/block/labeled — any may narrow `e`) OR any reassignment of `e`; emits at `e` used as a property/element-access receiver, a call/new callee, or a `++`/`--` operand; within a straight-line expr it skips the narrowed RHS of `&&`/`||`/`??` and the `?:` branches whose guard references `e`; it does NOT descend into nested functions. This makes it FP-safe WITHOUT the full flow graph (early-return guards + `if (typeof e === ...)` narrowing never fire because the walk stops at the control-flow statement). A dereference of the still-`unknown` value before any guard is always TS18046 in TS, so any matching baseline already carries it. Known FN (not FP): derefs AFTER a guard that TS would still flag.

- **TS6807 (shift simplification suggestion) is gated ENTIRELY on `@captureSuggestions` (the ONLY corpus test is `overshifts`) -> zero regression surface (B143, `checkShiftOverflow`)**: a shift `LHS <op> RHS` (`<<`/`>>`/`>>>`/`<<=`/`>>=`/`>>>=`) with a numeric-literal RHS `n` (optionally unary-`-`) where `n % 32 != n` suggests `LHS <op> (n%32)` (JS `%` keeps n's sign: `1<<-123`->`1<<-27`; |n|<32 is unchanged -> NOT flagged). Category = Error inside an enum-member initializer, Suggestion elsewhere (BaselineFormatter renders `category.name.lowercase()`, so suggestion/error categories work without any formatter change; suggestions are only INCLUDED because the formatter emits all diagnostics and `captureSuggestions` gates emission). Span = whole shift expr (`expr.pos`..`expressionTrueEnd`). **GOTCHA: the shift-op lookup must be a FUNCTION (`shiftOpText`), NOT a `private val` map — a field declared after `init{}` is null during the check pipeline (the recurring Kotlin init-order bit; cf. B135's `ARRAY_MUTATOR_METHODS`).**

- **TS2743 vs TS2558 for `new Map<1arg>()`/`new WeakMap<1arg>()` needs the lib constructor's IMPLICIT `new()` 0-type-arg overload, which the embedded lib omits (B144, `libCtorTypeParamRanges` + injection in `checkCallOrNewTypeArgCount`)**: the TS2743 overload-aware logic already existed (B95b) but derives per-overload type-param ranges from the SYMBOL's declarations — for `Map` that's only `interface Map<K,V>` (arity 2) + `declare var Map: MapConstructor` (our MapConstructor has ONLY `new()`, no generic `new<K,V>()`), so the range collapses to `[2..2]` -> TS2558 'Expected 2'. `libCtorTypeParamRanges` hardcodes the REAL construct-overload ranges (Map=`[0..0, 2..2]` -> `Map<1>` is TS2743 'either 0 or 2'; WeakMap=`[0..0, 0..2]` because its generic ctor's K/V both default -> `WeakMap<1>` is accepted, no error). Injected only when name∈{Map,WeakMap}, NO local shadow, NO user ClassDeclaration, and the lib-interface arity matches (==2) — FP-safe (only `new Map<1>()`/`>2` change; `new Map()`/`new Map<2>()` short-circuit before the override matters). Corpus has exactly 2 TS2743 baselines (`newMap` + `functionTypeArgumentArityErrors`).

### Lib-suggestion (TS2550/TS2583/TS2584/TS2585/TS2592) gotchas (round 135, B237–B242)

- **Adding a member to LIB_MIN_TARGET FILTERS it from the interface at unavailable lib levels — which SHIFTS every tuned "and N more" missing-property count involving that interface**: `RegExp.dotAll` regressed `assigningFromObjectToAnythingElse` ("and 11 more"→"10 more"); `Array.flat/flatMap` would shift the Blocker-#4 `genericArrayExtenstions` counts. For members whose PRESENCE is count-load-bearing, use **`LIB_MIN_TARGET_SOFT`**: consulted ONLY by access-site checks (member stays in the interface; property ACCESS still errors TS2550); the property-access-call TS2554 arity check is suppressed for soft-unavailable members. Before adding a HARD entry for a member that EXISTS in the embedded lib, grep the corpus for missing-property displays naming that interface.
- **All LIB_MIN_TARGET gates route through `libFeatureAvailable(intro)`**: empty `@lib` derives availability from `options.target` (harness default target is ES3, matching tsc); explicit `@lib` provides a feature iff some entry's BASE es-version ≥ intro (dotted entries count their prefix level — conservative towards suppression). Do NOT compare `options.target < minTarget` directly in new checks.
- **TS2583 name-availability is split across TWO mechanisms**: the es2015-era FORWARD_DECLARABLE set (`isLibTypeUnavailableEs2015` — Promise/Symbol EXCLUDED there: their TYPES live in lib.es5; their VALUES route through `libProvidesSymbolValue`/`libProvidesPromiseValue` → TS2585 via the TS2693 walker) and `LIB_GLOBAL_INTRODUCING` for later globals (Atomics es2017, AsyncGenerator es2018, BigInt es2020 …) with per-name dotted home-libs. `libUnavailableGlobalSuggestion(name)` is the shared entry; it also SUPPRESSES the TypeReference TS2314 arity check (TS2583 owns the position), and `getReturnTypeOfNewExpression` returns anyType for unavailable callees (else `m.clear()` FPs against the Constructor interface). `Proxy` is deliberately in NO map — tsc's feature map lacks it, so it gets plain TS2304 via a scope.has bypass.
- **`builtinLibDecls` holds top-level statements AND the inner VariableDeclaration nodes**: a `declare var Map: MapConstructor` lib statement binds its SYMBOL's declarations to the inner `VariableDeclaration`, not the statement — `decl !in builtinLibDecls` "user-declared?" identity checks silently mis-fire for lib var globals without the inner nodes (this blocked both Map value-position TS2583 and console TS2584).
- **The TS2550 lookup needs RECEIVER-SHAPE coverage, not just map entries**: checkMemberAccessMissing consults LIB_MIN_TARGET in per-shape branches — string-literal receivers; array-literal receivers; Identifier receivers (a bare lib identifier like `Array` resolves to the INSTANCE interface, so statics need the `<Name>Constructor.<prop>` fallback key — the embedded lib deliberately has NO ArrayConstructor); NewExpression lib-ctor receivers (`declare var X: XConstructor` Variable symbols + TYPED_ARRAY_NAMES/`Intl.X` name-convention; display `<any>`→`<unknown>`, typed arrays append `<ArrayBuffer>`); CallExpression results (symbol intrinsic → Symbol-iface key; nullable unions strip null/undefined to a single named interface); regex-literal receivers; the namespace Module branch (`Intl.PluralRules` → TS2550 'typeof Intl'). When a TS2550 mysteriously doesn't fire, identify WHICH shape the receiver is and bisect that branch with a marker diagnostic (code 29999).

### Module resolution diagnostic gotchas

- **`typeof import("spec")` parses as `TypeQuery(exprName = ImportType)`, NOT as `ImportType(isTypeOf=true)` (B174)**: the Parser's Typeof branch wraps the ImportType in a TypeQuery and `isTypeOf` stays false. Any checker branch matching "typeof import" type args/annotations must unwrap BOTH shapes (`(t as? ImportType) ?: (t as? TypeQuery)?.exprName as? ImportType`). Symptom of matching only ImportType: the branch silently never fires (the B174 marker-diagnostic trace found this).
- **An explicit `undefined` argument is LEGAL for an OPTIONAL parameter (B176, `allArgumentsMatch`)**: absent and undefined are interchangeable for parameters (exactOptionalPropertyTypes does NOT apply to params). The overload matcher accepts `undefined` args against `questionToken` params; without this, an overload PAIR like `toSpliced(start, deleteCount, ...items)` / `toSpliced(start, deleteCount?)` FP's TS2769 on `f(2, undefined)` against BOTH overloads. If you add per-arg checks to another overload path, mirror the gate.
- **A source member declared ONLY `static` does NOT satisfy an instance-side requirement (B175, `collectMissingProperties`)**: statics live in BOTH `members` and `staticMembers` (the bifurcation model), so name-presence over-counts — `class C { static prop() {} }` instances have NO `prop`. The missing-prop collector checks `srcSym.declarations.all { Static in modifiers }`. Also: a bare CLASS identifier in VALUE position is its STATIC side (`typeof B`) — the B175 branch in `checkAssignmentExpression` checks target instance-props against `classMemberNamesTransitive(staticSide=true)`, squiggles the RHS (TS reports the source expr there), and adds TS6213 "Did you mean to use 'new'?" only when the INSTANCE side would satisfy. The var-decl B87.4b gate is `(!canUse || isAssignable)` — running the static-aware check when the relation PASSED is what catches `var b: B = new C()` (the engine wrongly counts the static), while relation-failed keeps the standard path (no double-emit).


- **Declaration-emit nameability (TS2883 / TS4023 / TS2527) is a family of self-contained AST+module-resolution checks, NONE touching the type engine (B158/B159/B160, round 130, all in `checkDeclarationEmitNameability` + `checkDeclarationEmitComputedSymbolNameability`, pipeline steps 14a/14a', ALSO run under the `declarationOnly`/emitDeclarationOnly checker)**: when an EXPORTED annotation-less const's inferred type references a type that can't be written portably in a `.d.ts`. **TS2883** (`checkDeclarationEmitNameability`): `export const x = importedFn()` whose callee's explicit return type names a type in a NESTED node_modules package not reachable from the importer — `resolveBareViaNodeModules` walks the dir tree for `<dir>/node_modules/<spec>` (the main resolver does NOT do node_modules walking), `isFileNameableFrom` = the dir hosting the type file's LAST `node_modules/` segment must be an ancestor-or-equal of the importer's dir (top-level node_modules → always nameable; a package's private nested node_modules → nameable only from inside it). **TS4023** (`checkDeclarationEmitComputedSymbolNameability`): `export const x = {...typedExpr}` whose type has a computed-name member `[Sym]`/`[NS.sym]` keyed by a symbol from a non-value-accessible module — **the symbol firewall `computedKeyResolvesToSymbol` is load-bearing**: the key must resolve to a `Symbol()`/`Symbol.for()`-init or `unique symbol`-typed decl, else an ENUM-member key (`[Foo.Enum]`→TS2464) or undefined key (`[Enum.A]`→TS2304) FP's (the Enum2/Enum3 regressions). **TS2527**: `export const A1 = A` (imported) whose type carries a NESTED `unique symbol` (a type-literal property type, NOT the value's own top-level type — a top-level `unique symbol` is accessible via `typeof value`, so `typeAnnotationHasInaccessibleUniqueSymbol`'s `topLevel` flag suppresses it). **`isValueAccessibleIn` must NOT consult `globals`** (binder merges all file locals into it — Blocker #3 — so a symbol exported from ANOTHER module wrongly counts accessible); use KNOWN_GLOBALS. Remaining decl-emit-nameability tests (Object.assign default-export, package.json-exports `declarationEmitUsingTypeAlias1`, symlink, `#private`-field ES2015-downlevel-emit, mixin-inheritance TS4094) each need bespoke infra and are deferred.
- **isolatedModules re-export-of-type (TS1205/TS1269/TS1448) reuses the existing `isExportedNameTypeOnly`/`isTypeOnlyExportName` helpers and discriminates by which is true (B161, round 130, `checkIsolatedModulesReExportType` + require-form extension of `checkIsolatedModulesExportImportIsType`)**: under `isolatedModules && !verbatimModuleSyntax`, re-exporting a type-only name without `export type` is ambiguous to a single-file transpiler. For a non-type-only ExportSpecifier (`export {X} from "m"` OR local `export {X}` where X is a NON-type-only named import via `findNonTypeOnlyImport`), gate on `isExportedNameTypeOnly(srcName, srcSpec)`; then **`isTypeOnlyExportName` true → TS1448** (type-only-ness comes from an `export type {}` re-export → + related TS1377 "X was exported here" at the source specifier), **else → TS1205** (a direct type alias/interface). Span = the WHOLE ExportSpecifier (`T as T4`, collapses to the name when no rename). TS1269 require-form: `isRequireModuleTypeOnly` = the module's `export = T` target is a type alias/interface (not a value). FP-safe: skips .d.ts / type-only specifiers / type-only imports (`import type`) / namespace imports.
- **TS2741 for `typeof <moduleAliasA> = <moduleAliasB>` (module-namespace vs `typeof export=class`) is a SELF-CONTAINED AST SHAPE, NOT a real namespace `Type` in the relation engine (B155, `moduleAliasTypeofShape` + `tryEmitModuleNamespaceTs2741`)**: `typeofExternalModules`/`typeofAmbientExternalModules` — `var y1: typeof ext = ext; y1 = exp;` where `ext`=`import ext = require('./external')` (a normal module `export class C`) and `exp`=`import exp = require('./exportAssign')` (`export = D`, D a class). `moduleAliasTypeofShape(sym, contextFile)` returns `(memberName -> name-decl-pos-or-null, displayString)`: an `export = X` (X a module-local class) → the static side `typeof X` = synthetic `prototype` (null pos → no TS2728) + X's STATIC members; a normal module → its exported VALUE names (class/function/var/enum) displayed `typeof import("<base>")`. A dedicated branch at the TOP of the `target is Identifier` case in `checkAssignmentExpression` (gated `expr.right is Identifier`) resolves the LHS var's `typeof <alias>` annotation subject + the RHS alias to two shapes, finds the FIRST target member absent from source, emits TS2741 "Property 'X' is missing in type '<sourceDisplay>' but required in type '<targetDisplay>'." + TS2728 if the missing member has a name-decl pos. **Why NOT a real `Type`:** the queue spec wanted `typeof <module>` modeled as a namespace `Type.Object` flowing through `collectMissingProperties`/assignability — rated MEDIUM-risk because namespace-as-type flows broadly. The AST-shape approach has ZERO general-engine blast radius (the shape is never a `Type` the relation engine sees) and flipped both tests. One helper covers the ambient sibling (`typeofAmbientExternalModules` = same shape + already-emitted TS2564). If you extend to namespace-import (`import * as`) or `export default` module shapes, extend `moduleAliasTypeofShape`, not the relation engine.
- **TS2349 "...Type 'typeof import(\"mod\")' has no call signatures." for CALLING a CJS-default-as-namespace (B154/B154b, `cjsDefaultNsShapes` + early branch in `checkSingleCallExpressionTypes`)**: a CJS module's `default` export, when imported, is the WHOLE `module.exports` NAMESPACE (`typeof import("mod")`), NOT the inner value — so calling it has no call signatures. TWO gated shapes: **(nodenext)** an ESM importer (`.mts`/`.mjs`, `effectiveModule.isNodeNext`) default-importing a `.cts`/`.cjs` module with a DIRECT `export default` (`ExportAssignment` `isExportEquals=false`); **(commonjs)** `@module commonjs + esModuleInterop` with a `.ts` importer where the imported module uses `export = Y` and `Y` is `import Y = require("./Z")` (a require-alias to a proper NAMESPACE module Z — validated by `isProperNamespaceModule`: has ESM/`export default` exports and NO `export =`). `cjsDefaultNsShapes(fileName)` (memoized) builds, per importer file, the local default-binding names (`import a from`/`import c,{}`/`import {default as b}`) AND namespace-import members re-exporting such a default (`import * as self` + `export {default[ as def]} from "./X"`). The early branch fires TS2349 at the call site (Identifier callee → whole-name span; `ns.member()` → member span). **FP firewall (load-bearing):** nodenext path requires CJS-ext target + direct `export default` (a `.mts`→`.mts` ESM-default IS the value, callable); commonjs path requires the `export =`→require-alias→proper-namespace CHAIN (direct `export default` under esModuleInterop+commonjs gives the VALUE via `__importDefault`, callable; `export = fn`/`export = class` give a callable — both excluded). Fires only on DIRECT calls. **DO NOT broaden the gate to all commonjs default-imports** — the chain requirement is what keeps the FP surface narrow (per the passing-set argument: TS always errors this exact shape).
- **TS5097 ("import path can only end with '.ts' when allowImportingTsExtensions is enabled") has TWO emission branches in the import-specifier walker (Checker.kt ~23362, B141)**: (1) the original RELATIVE branch (`./foo.ts`); (2) the BARE branch for a `paths`-mapped specifier ending in `.ts`/`.tsx`. The bare branch approximates TS's **resolvedUsingTsExtension** rule with TWO load-bearing checks: the longest-prefix-matching `paths` pattern KEY must NOT itself end in the extension (`"baz/*.ts"` absorbs the `.ts` -> no error), AND a substituted `paths` target must end in `.ts`/`.tsx` AND directly name an existing source file in `fileResults` (use the DIRECT-key forms `t`/`/t`/`./t`, NOT `resolveModuleSpecifier` which does directory-index resolution -- else a package-dir name like `zone.tsx/index.d.ts` matched by `"*":["foo/*"]` wrongly fires TS5097). Both checks are required: dropping the file-resolution gate FP'd `pathMappingBasedModuleResolution_withExtensionInName`; the key-ext check is TS's pattern-absorption rule.

- **TS2694 ("Namespace 'X' has no exported member 'Y'.") for a type ref `X.Y` INSIDE a `declare module "m" { ... }` body where `X` is a MODULE-LOCAL namespace is a PURELY AST-BASED check (`checkAmbientModuleLocalNamespaceMemberRefs`, B146), NOT symbol-table-based**: a module-local `namespace X { export interface foo }` shadows a file-level `declare namespace X { export interface bar }`, so `X.bar` inside the module is TS2694 — but the global symbol-merge UNIFIES the inner/outer `X` (both named `X`), so a symbol lookup would wrongly see `bar`. The check therefore collects the local namespace's member names DIRECTLY from its body AST (`collectNamespaceLocalMemberNames`, exported-or-not for FP-safety) and walks the module body's type annotations (`forEachQualifiedTypeRefInStatement`/`Type`/`ClassElement`) for 2-segment `Root.member` refs (deeper `A.B.member` chains are FN-skipped). FP-safe: fires only when `Root` is a module-local namespace, `Root` is not also bound to a non-namespace value/alias in the body (`import =`, `export { Y as X }` rename — but NOT a plain `export { X }` re-export), and `member` is absent from EVERY local declaration of `Root`. **Only flips the SINGLE-FILE case** — the cross-FILE sibling (`exportSpecifierReferencingOuterDeclaration4`, two file-level `declare namespace X` in different files that merge via `mergeSymbolTable`) stays failing (Blocker #3). The `export { Y as X }` value-alias→TS2503 case (`exportSpecifierAndLocalMemberDeclaration`) is a SEPARATE mechanism, not handled here.
- **TS1203/TS1202 (`export =`/`import = require()` "cannot be used when targeting ECMAScript modules") and TS1192 ("no default export") treat a `.mts`/`.mjs`/`.d.mts` file as an ES module ONLY under node module kinds (`effectiveModule.isNodeNext`), NOT under commonjs/amd/system/umd (B145)**: the `.mts`-is-ESM rule comes from `impliedNodeFormat`, which is computed only under node resolution. Under amd/system/umd (module kind < ES2015, non-node) the GLOBAL module setting governs and `export =`/`import = require()` in a `.mts` is LEGAL — gating `fileIsMtsEsm`/`targetIsEsm` on `isNodeNext` is load-bearing (an unconditional `.mts`-is-ESM check FP'd TS1202 on `impliedNodeFormatEmit1`'s `/h.mts` under amd/system/umd, where the baseline shows `0 errors`). `checkExportAssignmentInEsModule` also bypasses the plain-`.d.ts` skip for `.d.mts` (a `.d.mts` ESM declaration may NOT use `export =`, unlike a CJS-ambient `.d.ts`). `checkDefaultImports` must NOT globally early-return on `allowSyntheticDefaultImports`: synthetic defaults synthesize a default only for CJS-format targets (the whole `module.exports`), so an ESM-format node-mode target with no `export default` is plain TS1192 even with `allowSyntheticDefaultImports`/`esModuleInterop` (the per-import `targetIsEsm` gate bypasses ALL CJS-synthetic-default suppression incl. the export=→TS1259 path). `resolveRelativeIncludingIndex` carries `.d.mts`/`.d.cts` exts and is the checkDefaultImports resolution fallback so a runtime `.mjs` specifier resolves to its `.d.mts` declaration sibling; the TS1192 module-name display strips a trailing module extension for ESM targets only (`"./other.mjs"` -> `"other"`).

### Module detection gotchas

- **`checkJs` implies `allowJs`, and MULTI-FILE test options BYPASS `parseCompilerOptions` (B98.r165)**: TS's `getAllowJSCompilerOption` returns `allowJs ?? !!checkJs` — a `@checkJs`-only program (no `@allowJs`) still loads+checks its `.js` files. Our `applyImpliedAllowJs` (CompilerOptions.kt) does this and MUST be called at ALL THREE option-finalization points, because the SINGLE-file path uses `parseCompilerOptions` but the MULTI-file path (`@filename:` present → `parsed.hasExplicitFilenames`) builds its options inside `parseMultiFileSource`'s OWN `applyDirective` loop and never calls `parseCompilerOptions`. The driver also re-applies it after `optionOverrides`. Symptom of getting this wrong: a multi-file `@checkJs`-no-`@allowJs` test's `.js` files are absent from `parsedSourceFiles`/`binderResults` → the checker emits NOTHING ("none produced"). Any future option-derivation rule (implied defaults) needs the same all-three-sites treatment.
- **Debugging "is this checker path reached?": gradle SUPPRESSES test stdout/stderr** (no `testLogging.showStandardStreams` in build.gradle.kts), AND the forked-JVM stderr does NOT land in the test XML's `<system-err>`. A `System.err.println` trace is therefore INVISIBLE under `./gradlew jvmTest`. To trace whether a check runs, emit a MARKER DIAGNOSTIC (`diagnostics.add(... code=29999 ...)`) — it surfaces in the `errorsMatchBaseline` expected-vs-actual diff. Also note: the Checker `init` gates most checks behind `if (!declarationOnly)`; `@emitDeclarationOnly` multi-file runs a `declarationOnly=true` checker that skips them.
- **TS2855 (`super.X` of a parent class FIELD) is a JS-only AST walker (`checkClassFieldSuperAccessJs`, B98.r165)**: class fields (own-instance, incl. `this.X=`/`this.X;`/`this['X']` expando + `accessor`-less PropertyDeclarations) are NOT on the prototype, so `super.field` is always an error. Collect parent fields MINUS prototype members (methods/get-set/`accessor` auto-props), then flag derived-class `super.X`/`super['X']` against the field set. String-literal-keyed fields (`this['x']`) display QUOTED in the message (parent's declaration quote style, via `quotedName`). The shared `walkAccessesNoFnBoundary` descends through arrows + control flow but STOPS at nested non-arrow functions/methods/classes (which rebind `this`/`super`); it's a MEMBER fn (not local) so `waExpr`/`waStmt` can be mutually recursive (Kotlin local funs can't forward-reference).

- **`export as namespace X` has NO AST node — the parser MISPARSES it into a `namespace X` ModuleDeclaration (+ stray ExpressionStatement/EmptyStatement) (B98.r146)**: it is detected only by a source regex (`collectUmdGlobalsAndModuleFiles` / `checkUmdGlobalVsDeclareGlobalConst` / `checkExportAsNamespaceSelfCycle`). CONSEQUENCE: any walker that scans a file's top-level statements for a *genuine* declaration of X (e.g. "does this module locally declare X?") will be FOOLED by the misparsed `namespace X` ModuleDeclaration produced by the `export as namespace X;` line itself. Exclude it by skipping statements whose `.pos` falls within the `export as namespace X` regex-match source span (`stmt.pos in match.range`). This is exactly what made the FIRST cut of `checkExportAsNamespaceSelfCycle` (TS2303 `export = X` + `export as namespace X` self-cycle, pipeline 56c) silently emit nothing — gate (c) saw the misparse as a real local `namespace X` and bailed. The legit-UMD firewall (`export = Foo; export as namespace Foo;` where Foo is a real module-local `declare namespace Foo`/`import * as Foo` → NOT circular) depends on this exclusion being precise.
- **TS1147 walker covers BOTH `ImportEqualsDeclaration` AND `ImportDeclaration` inside namespace bodies (B68.1)**: `walkRequireImportInNamespace` handles all three import forms: `import = require("X")`, `import * as N from "X"`, `import N from "X"`, `import {n} from "X"`, `import "X"`. The walker bails for `declare global` and string-literal-named namespaces (those are module augmentations with different diagnostics). When extending, mirror across both branches — the gate is identical (`inNamespace` boolean threaded through ModuleDeclaration recursion).
- **TS2567 enum-merge detection lives in THREE walkers, each for a disjoint shape (B88.1)**: (1) the per-file walker (Checker.kt:~18421) handles same-file top-level declaration groups; (2) `checkCrossFileEnumConflicts` (~77499) handles SCRIPT files only (skips module files) and only DIRECT top-level declarations — no module-specifier resolution; (3) `checkModuleAugmentationEnumMerge` (~77640) handles `declare module "X" { export enum E }` augmentations whose partner is reached via `resolveModuleSpecifier` + `findExportedDeclAcrossReexports` (follows `export * from` / `export {…} from` chains). When extending enum-merge detection, pick the walker matching the shape — don't broaden (2) to module files (it would FP on legitimate module augmentations); add a new gated branch to (3) instead.
- **Augmentation-vs-definition is distinguished by ABSENCE of an inner `export =`, NOT by `isModuleFile` (B90.1)**: `checkModuleAugmentationOfNonModuleEntity` (TS2671 "Cannot augment module 'X' because it resolves to a non-module entity") must process the AUGMENTATION block while skipping the DEFINITION block — both are `declare module "X"` and may live in any file. The DEFINITION carries the `export = …`; the augmentation does not. So the walker's skip gate is `body.statements.any { it is ExportAssignment && it.isExportEquals }` (skip = it's the definition). The shared detector `ambientModuleExportEqualsIsValueOnly(specifier)` returns true only when the `export = name` target is declared in-block as a `var`/`function` ONLY (no class/interface/type-alias/enum/namespace) via `isNameValueOnlyInBlock` — that "value-only" gate is the FP firewall (legitimate `export = namespace/class` augmentations don't trip it). The SAME detector drives the paired TS2503 in `checkTypeNameResolved`'s QualifiedName branch (`x.A` where `x` is an `import x = require("X")` alias to a value-only-`export=` module) — that emit MUST sit BEFORE the existing `!Module`/TS2702 path (x may carry a Module flag from the augmentation merge, which would otherwise short-circuit it) and is gated on `leftSym is Alias` + `getImportEqualsSpecifier`, so it never fires for plain undeclared names (those take the pre-existing `!scope.has` TS2503 branch).
- **TS2303 "Circular definition of import alias" lives in THREE disjoint emission sites (B91.1)**: (1) `checkCircularImportAlias` (Checker.kt:~43476) — entity-name cycles `import X = Y.Z` (gate: `moduleReference is Identifier`), recurses into namespaces/blocks but SKIPS `.d.ts` files; (2) `emitTS2303ForImportEquals` (~13208, called from `checkTypeNameResolved`) — `import X = <bare-identifier>` whose ref is unresolvable AND the alias is re-exported under `declaration:true`; (3) `checkCircularExportEqualsImportAlias` (~43587, pipeline step 56b) — `import self = require("M"); export = self;` EXTERNAL-module-reference cycles across file modules AND ambient `declare module "X"` bodies (including in `.d.ts`). All three are disjoint by `moduleReference` kind / context — pick the matching one when extending. For (3): builds a `file:`/`ambient:`-keyed registry of self-export modules, follows the `require → export=self` chain (bare spec → ambient key; relative → `resolveModuleSpecifierRelative`), detects cycles. **Report-position rule (load-bearing, matches TypeScript):** the cycle "entry" = the member imported by an `import = require` whose container is NOT in the cycle; AMBIENT entry → report the entry's own self-import; FILE entry → report the entry's PREDECESSOR (the self-import whose `require` points back to entry). Squiggle spans the import declaration INCLUDING the trailing `;`. Gate requires a genuine cycle AND an external importer → zero FP surface (legit non-cyclic `import x = require; export = x` re-exports never trip it).
- **Cross-file MERGED-interface duplicate-identifier conflicts (B92, `checkCrossFileInterfaceMemberConflicts` Checker.kt:~77971, pipeline step 73f)**: when the same interface name is declared in 2 files sharing a scope (global script scope; `declare global { }`; `declare module "X" { }`) and a member is a PROPERTY in one file + a METHOD in another, that's a hard TS2300 conflict. **Property-vs-property is deliberately NOT detected** (identical-type merges are legal; different-type → TS2717 not TS2300) — only property-vs-method, to keep the FP surface zero. **Collapse threshold (load-bearing magic number, matches TypeScript's `amalgamatedDuplicates` reporting):** TypeScript amalgamates these errors per ordered file-pair, then if `conflictingSymbols.size < 8` → per-member TS2300 + related TS6203 "'X' was also declared here."; if `>= 8` → ONE collapsed TS6200 "Definitions of the following identifiers conflict ...: a, b, c" per file (at the file's first non-trivia token via `firstTokenSpanOfFile` — `interface`→9 / `declare`→7 / `class`→5) + related TS6201 "Conflicts are in this file." Top-level interfaces are counted into the `global` scope ONLY in non-module (script) files (module-local interfaces don't merge across files). The VALUE-identifier cross-file cases (`class A` in 2 files → collapsed TS6200; `class`/`type`/`var` mixes + TS6204 "and here") are Blocker #3-adjacent and NOT handled here (B92d).
- **Cross-file MIXED class/type-alias/const-let identifier conflicts use the HUB model, NOT per-pair amalgamation (B93a, `checkCrossFileIdentifierConflicts` Checker.kt:~77810, pipeline step 73a2)**: handles top-level SCRIPT-file (non-module, non-.d.ts) names where a class / type-alias mixes with const/let (or ≥2 type-aliases) — the cases 73b (pure const/let), 73g (pure class-vs-class) and the previously-absent cross-file type-alias checker all missed. Emits PER SPACE: value-space occupiers (class + const + let), type-space occupiers (class + type-alias). A space conflicts when ≥2 occupiers span ≥2 files; code = TS2451 if any value-space decl is block-scoped (const/let), else TS2300; type-space is always TS2300. **HUB model (load-bearing, matches TS `mergeSymbol` + `lookupOrIssueError` dedup):** the FIRST-processed declaration (source order = `binderResults` order then statement order) is the hub; its single diagnostic accumulates related infos TS6203 (first other) then TS6204 (each subsequent other); every OTHER declaration emits its own diagnostic relating back to ONLY the hub with a single TS6203. So for `Foo` = class(file1)+type(file2)+type(file3): file1 gets TS6203 file2 + TS6204 file3, file2 & file3 each get just TS6203 file1. Shared `emitCrossFileHubDuplicates(ordered, code, message)` does this. **Narrow gate (FP firewall):** every decl of the name ∈ {class,type-alias,const,let} (any var/function/interface/namespace/enum decl → bail, those merge); ≤1 class (≥2 → 73g owns it); must involve a type-alias OR a class+block mix (pure const/let → 73b owns it). **Double-emit coordination:** value-space block-scoped names handled here are added to the checker field `crossFileIdentifierHandledBlockNames`; 73b skips any name in that set. Does NOT handle augmentation / UMD-namespace bodies (`export as namespace`, `declare global { namespace }`, `declare module "X"`) — that's the still-failing `exportAsNamespace_augment` (B93b).
- **`BaselineFormatter` pretty multi-file footer uses MIXED line endings (B92)**: the `Errors  Files` per-file summary table (emitted only when `pretty && errorCount>1 && distinctFiles>1`) has the `Found N errors in M files.` line + the blank separator line ending in CRLF (`\r\n`), but `Errors  Files` and each `<count.padStart(6)>  <file>:<firstLine>` row end in LF only (`\n`). This is TypeScript's actual byte output (verified via `od -c`) — don't "normalize" them to all-CRLF or the 9 footer-baselines (dup-identifier family + `manyCompilerErrorsInTheTwoFiles` + `typedefCrossModule5`) won't match.
- **TS2484 re-export conflict walker (B68.2 + B68.5)**: `checkExportConflictInNamespace` delegates to `checkExportConflictInScope` which pre-computes `Map<namespaceName, Set<exportedNames>>` per scope. Recurses into nested namespace bodies (each namespace body is its own scope with its own merged-exports map). Covers `namespace Outer { namespace M { export var x } namespace M { export {x} } }` shape as well as file-scope. Squiggle lands on the ExportSpecifier's name identifier.
- **Index signature param type validity (B68.4)**: When the index sig param type is an invalid `KeywordTypeNode` (`any`/`boolean`/`void`/etc., not `string`/`number`/`symbol`), the Parser SKIPS the TS1021 "must have a type annotation" emission and the Checker emits TS1268 instead (mirroring TypeScript — they don't double-report). The Checker walker `checkIndexSigInStatement` covers class / interface / module / TypeAliasDeclaration / VariableStatement TypeLiteral annotations.
- **`moduleDetection: "force"`** makes ALL files modules regardless of content. Both `isModuleFile()` (Transformer) and `hasModuleStatements()` (Emitter) check for this.
- **`@module: none` + `@outFile` bundling rules**: (a) auxiliary `.js` files with `import`/`export` statements are NOT bundled into the outFile output — TypeScript treats them as type-info-only / allowJs-checking-only. Phase 3 of `TypeScriptCompiler.kt` skips them via `continue`. (b) Native `import()` syntax is preserved verbatim when target≥ES2020 (no CJS rewrite). For target<ES2020, the dynamic import is rewritten to `Promise.resolve().then(() => __importStar(require(...)))` AND the `./` prefix is stripped from the require path (no module resolver runtime under `module: none`). Both pieces live in `Transformer.kt`'s `transformToCommonJS` / `buildCjsDynamicImport`.
- **`.mts`/`.mjs`/`.cts`/`.cjs` extensions** are always module files. Both functions also check for these extensions.
- **`isolatedModules: true` ≠ `moduleDetection: force`**: `isolatedModules` tells TypeScript to check each file independently but does NOT force module treatment for files without imports/exports. Adding `isModuleFile = true` for `isolatedModules` causes regressions.
- **Node16/Node18/Node20/NodeNext default to CJS for `.ts` files (UNLESS a `package.json` declares `"type": "module"`)**: `isESModuleFormat` returns `false` for plain `.ts` files BY DEFAULT — only `.mts`/`.mjs` are unconditionally ESM. The `(options, fileName)` overload consults `options.packageJsonTypes` (populated by `collectPackageJsonTypes` from multi-file source `package.json` files outside `node_modules/`), walking from the file's directory upward to find the nearest enclosing `"type"` field. Use the `options`-aware overload in any new code that determines ESM vs CJS under nodenext — the legacy `(module, fileName)` overload has NO package.json context. Map keys preserve leading `/` (absolute paths) and use `""` for the implicit root.
- **JSON files re-emitted with trailing comma stripping**: `TypeScriptCompiler.kt` strips trailing commas from JSON output using `stripJsonTrailingCommas()` since TypeScript parses and re-emits JSON, naturally removing them.
- **`esModuleInterop` defaults to `true`**: TypeScript 5.5+ deprecated `esModuleInterop: false`. Test baselines without explicit `@esModuleInterop` expect helpers (`__importStar`, `__importDefault`). Only when `@esModuleInterop: false` is explicitly set should helpers be skipped for default/namespace imports.
- **`__importStar`/`__importDefault` conditional on `esModuleInterop`**: These helpers wrap `require()` only when `esModuleInterop: true`. Without it, use plain `require()`. `__exportStar`/`__createBinding` are ALWAYS used for `export * from` regardless of `esModuleInterop`.
- **Helper ordering depends on first usage**: When both `__importStar` and `__exportStar` are needed, TypeScript emits the one used first in the output before the other. Track `importStarUsedFirst` by checking which `needsXxx = true` is set first.
- **`importHelpers: true` uses tslib**: When set, don't emit inline helper functions. Instead add `const tslib_1 = require("tslib")` (CJS) or `"tslib"` dep + `tslib_1` param (AMD), and use `tslib_1.__helperName(...)` instead of bare `__helperName(...)`. The `helperExpr()` method handles this.
- **TS2354 "module 'tslib' cannot be found" resolves tslib PER-FILE, not program-wide (B98.r163)**: `checkImportHelpersWithoutTslib`'s `tslibResolvableFor(fileName)` walks to the nearest enclosing `node_modules/` (baseDir = the path substring BEFORE `node_modules/`, prefix-matched against the file path — same nearest-enclosing model as `resolveTslibDedupKey`). A `node_modules/tslib` under `/package1` does NOT satisfy a file in `/package2`; a ROOT `node_modules/tslib` (baseDir `""`/`"/"`) is an ancestor of everything so it satisfies all files. **Match `lastIndexOf("node_modules/")` NOT `"/node_modules/"`** — fixtures mix leading-slash conventions (`importHelpers.ts` → `node_modules/tslib/index.d.ts`, `tslibNotFoundDifferentModules` → `/package1/node_modules/tslib/...`); the no-slash form must still match (within one test the file paths share the convention, so the baseDir prefix-match stays sound). Do NOT revert to the old program-wide `hasTslib` boolean — it suppressed TS2354 for tslib-less packages whenever ANY package had tslib.
- **TS2343 "missing tslib helper" for `__awaiter`/`__generator` is reported ONCE PER RESOLVED TSLIB INSTALL per helper** (B98.r28 corrected the earlier "once per program" model): the FIRST construct needing a missing helper errors for that install, then later uses RESOLVING TO THE SAME tslib install are suppressed; a DIFFERENT install (e.g. a per-package `node_modules/tslib`) reports independently. Baselines: `tslibMissingHelper` (one shared `/node_modules/tslib`) reports once; `tslibMultipleMissingHelper` (two per-package installs) reports once each. The field `reportedMissingTslibHelpers: MutableSet<String>` is keyed `"<tslibKey>|<helper>"` where tslibKey comes from `resolveTslibDedupKey(fileName, …)` (nearest enclosing `node_modules/tslib` dir, or `"ambient"`/`"global"`). The OLDER helper emissions in `checkStmtForMissingHelper` (`__exportStar`/`__extends`/`__rest`/`__asyncGenerator`/`__await`/`__decorate`/…) do NOT dedup — they pass only because their fixtures have a single occurrence. If you add a helper check OR extend `__awaiter` to async methods/arrows, gate on the install-keyed `reportedMissingTslibHelpers` or a multi-occurrence test gets duplicate TS2343. (`__rest` is emitted for object-rest binding patterns in BOTH variable declarations and FunctionDeclaration parameters, the latter gated `target < ES2018`.)
- **`exprContainsDynamicImport` must mirror `rewriteCjsDynExpr`**: The detection function (used by `isModuleFile`) must handle ALL expression types that the rewriting function handles. Missing `PropertyAccessExpression` caused `import("./foo").then(...)` to not be detected as a module file, so `transformToCommonJS` was never called. Both functions must handle: PropertyAccessExpression, ElementAccessExpression, ConditionalExpression, YieldExpression, NewExpression, SpreadElement, ArrayLiteralExpression, PrefixUnaryExpression, PostfixUnaryExpression.
- **`Emitter.hasModuleStatements` must mirror `Transformer.isModuleFile` for dynamic imports**: `Emitter.hasModuleStatements` decides whether to skip the top-level `"use strict";` for AMD/UMD/System module files. It must recognize dynamic `import()` calls as module signals — otherwise a file with ONLY `import("x")` (no traditional import/export) gets BOTH the System transform's inner `"use strict"` AND a stray top-level `"use strict";` emitted before `System.register(...)`. The Emitter has its own `statementContainsDynamicImport`/`expressionContainsDynamicImport` walkers (cannot share Transformer's because they're in different files); when adding new module-signal detection to `Transformer.isModuleFile`, mirror it to `Emitter.hasModuleStatements`.
- **`resolveModuleSpecifier` intentionally does NOT try `.js`/`.jsx` extensions**: Doing so globally causes TS2459 false-positives (our CJS/`module.exports` export analysis is incomplete) and other cross-file lookup regressions. For a specific check that needs JS-aware resolution under `allowJs`/`checkJs`, add a SCOPED helper (e.g. `resolvesAsJsOrJsx` used by `checkAmbientModuleAugmentations`) rather than modifying the main resolver.
- **The node/commonjs relative-missing TS2307 gate (B98.r1, Checker.kt:~20527) is gated to EXPLICIT `@module: commonjs` only, NOT the default-null module / `effectiveModuleRes == "node10"`**: broadening to node10 (which the no-`@module` default maps to) re-exposes the resolver's gaps on the large pool of multi-file fixtures with relative imports that legitimately resolve. The gate is backed by `resolveRelativeIncludingIndex` (a DELIBERATELY-more-permissive "does this relative specifier resolve to ANY file?" check — tries every module extension incl. `.js/.jsx/.json`, both `./`-prefixed and unprefixed `fileResults` keys, and `<spec>/index.<ext>`) — finding a `.js`/`.jsx`/`.tsx` sibling must SUPPRESS TS2307 because TS resolves those (as untyped module / with TS6142, never TS2307). It is also gated by `hasTsErrorSuppressionAbove` (the ONLY directive-suppression in the codebase — a narrow line-scan for `@ts-expect-error`/`@ts-ignore` on the import line or the line above; we have no general directive-suppression model). Residual known-FP: a `.js` target with NO `allowJs` (the `.js` file isn't loaded into `fileResults`) — left as noise on already-failing tests rather than risk modeling untyped-`.js` resolution.
- **ALL file locals merged into globals at Checker init** (`mergeSymbolTable(globals, result.locals)` for every binderResult): This conflates script-file locals (legitimately global) with module-file locals (should require an explicit import to be visible). Consequence: in file X, an identifier exported from an unrelated module file Y appears in X's scope chain via `scope.has(name)`. This blocks fine-grained module-visibility diagnostics. Splitting "true globals" from module-file locals would unblock several tests but has broad regression risk and needs per-file scope construction.

### Cross-file infrastructure gotchas

- **`mergeSymbolTable` mutates the existing target symbol's `declarations` list**: When `target[name]` already exists, the helper does `existing.flags |= symbol.flags; existing.declarations.addAll(symbol.declarations)` — so calling it twice across the same `result.locals` corpus duplicates declarations on the SHARED symbol object. The init-block merge into `globals` already does this once for every cross-file same-name pair; any additional pass building per-file scope tables MUST NOT re-merge across binderResults via this helper. Use direct `map[name] = sym` assignment with first-write-wins for shared pools and last-write-wins for own-file overrides — no `addAll`, no symbol mutation. Failure mode is silent until a downstream check (e.g. TS6133 unused-T-param, declaration count) sees the duplicated declaration list and behaves incorrectly.
- **`isValueExport`/`isTypeOnlyExportName` cross-file lookups must NOT rely on symbol flags**: `mergeSymbolTable` pollutes the target file's `locals["X"]` symbol with flags merged in from importing files (e.g., `import { T } from "./type"; const T = 0` in file A causes /type.ts's T symbol to acquire BlockScopedVariable|Alias|ExportValue flags). Code that asks "is X exported from file Y as a value or type?" MUST scan `targetResult.sourceFile.statements` directly for declarations of X, not consult `targetResult.locals[X].flags`. Mirror pattern in `isValueExport` (Checker.kt:955) walks the AST and classifies each declaration's kind. Fall back to flag-based logic only when no direct declaration is found (ambient/re-export cases).

### Binder gotchas

- **`canMerge` must include Variable+Module**: `declare const b: T; declare namespace b {}` is valid TypeScript. The binder's `canMerge` must allow `Variable + Module` and `Module + Variable` merging, otherwise the second declaration silently overwrites the first symbol. This matters for `isTypeOnlyImportRequire` which then sees only the namespace and incorrectly elides the `require()`. **BUT (B98.r46): var+namespace merge is allowed ONLY when the namespace is VALUE-FREE (uninstantiated — only types/interfaces).** An INSTANTIATED namespace (one with value exports, e.g. `export var x`) is a SECOND VALUE binding → TS2300 even for `declare var` (`declare var console; namespace console { export var x }` conflicts). The `namespaceVarAllowed` gate (Checker.kt:~19710, duplicate-declaration TS2300/TS2451 path) is `group.filter{namespace}.all{ !isNamespaceInstantiated(it) }` — do NOT re-add a `|| allVarsDeclare` blanket allowance (the old comment "a declare var can merge with any namespace" was wrong; the empty-namespace `b{}` case survives because it's not instantiated).
- **`canMerge` must include Variable+Interface**: `interface Symbol {}` + `declare var Symbol: SymbolConstructor;` is the standard wrapper-type pattern in lib.d.ts. Without this merge, the var silently overwrites the interface — `Symbol` resolves to anyType in type position and `sym = Sym` skips type checking. Same gap blocks any user `class B extends A` where A is `interface A {}` + `declare var A: { new(): A }` (e.g. `staticMismatchBecauseOfPrototype`). Note: enabling this merge also makes lib types like `Object`/`Promise` resolve to real Type.Interface (was anyType), exposing two latent gaps in the relation engine — see `propertiesRelatedTo` OBJECT_PROTOTYPE_PROPERTIES filter and async return-type Promise unwrapping below.
- **Ambient module symbol overwritten by import alias**: `import x = require("X")` in the same file as `declare module "X"` creates an Alias symbol that overwrites the NamespaceModule in `locals["X"]` (Alias doesn't canMerge with Module). `isAmbientModuleTypeOnly` must analyze the ModuleBlock AST directly instead of looking up `locals[name]`.
- **Module augmentation vs definition**: `declare module "X"` in a module file (has imports/exports) is an augmentation. In a script file, it's a definition. `isAmbientModuleTypeOnly` must skip module files to avoid treating augmentations (which only add types) as the full module definition.
- **`SymbolFlags.ConstEnum` is set on namespaces holding only const enums**: `bindModuleDeclaration` sets `SymbolFlags.ConstEnum or NamespaceModule` when `ModuleInstanceState.ConstEnumOnly`. Cascades up: `namespace A { namespace B { namespace C { const enum E {...} } } }` makes A, B, C all carry `SymbolFlags.ConstEnum`. So `flags.hasAny(SymbolFlags.Enum)` (= ConstEnum or RegularEnum) returns TRUE for these namespaces. Any code that distinguishes "real enum" from "namespace" must check `declarations.any { it is EnumDeclaration }` rather than relying on the flag alone.
- **Block-scoped declarations are NOT bound** (B83.5, 2026-05-27): `Binder.kt:bindStatement` only dispatches symbol-declaration cases via explicit `when` arms (Variable/Function/Class/Interface/TypeAlias/Enum/Module/Import/Export). The catch-all `else` branch silently ignores `WhileStatement`/`Block`/`IfStatement`/`ForStatement`/`TryStatement`/`SwitchStatement` and every other non-declaration statement, so any `class X` / `interface I` / `type T` / `enum E` / `function F` declared INSIDE their bodies is NEVER bound to file `locals` or `globals`. Consequence: any checker walker that looks up such a declaration by name via `globals[name]` / `result.locals[name]` / `perFileScope[file]?.get(name)` returns null. Symptom: TS2339/TS2551/TS2693/TS2304 silently never fires inside block-scoped class bodies because `classType = null`. Surgical fix pattern when the AST is in-hand: synthesize a transient `Symbol(SymbolFlags.Class, stmt.name.text)` with `declarations = [stmt]` and pass to `getDeclaredTypeOfSymbol(symbol)`. The synthetic symbol must NOT be published to binder tables (`globals.put` / `result.locals.put`) — it's a checker-pass-local temporary; cross-decl merging or multi-pass identity is the binder's job. Used in `checkPropertyAccessInStatement`'s ClassDeclaration branch (Checker.kt:~61539); extend to similar `globals[stmt.name.text]`-based lookups if more shapes surface (other checker walkers that recurse into block bodies but resolve nested decls by name).

### Type system gotchas

- **Conditional-type `infer` binding is AST-guided positional unification, NOT type-level (B119)**: `U extends Synthetic<T, infer V> ? V : never` — `getTypeFromTypeNode(extendsType)` yields errorType for an infer-bearing extends-type, so `getTypeFromConditionalType` USED to return anyType (masking the inferred result). `tryEvaluateConditionalWithInfer` (Checker.kt, gates `getTypeFromConditionalType` BEFORE eager extends resolution) fires ONLY when (a) `node.extendsType` is a `TypeReference` with ≥1 top-level `InferType` arg, (b) checkType is a concrete `Type.Reference` to the SAME-named target (compare `checkRef.target.symbol?.name` == `getTypeReferenceLastName(extAst.typeName)`), (c) matching arity, (d) every non-infer position is `checkTypeRelatedTo(checkArg, patternArg, assignableRelation)`. It binds each `InferType` name → `checkRef.resolvedTypeArguments[i]`, then resolves `node.trueType` with the bindings layered onto `currentTypeAliasArgs` (the B50.1 vehicle — consulted by `getTypeFromTypeReference`'s bare-name lookup, and a non-null map bypasses the nodeTypes cache → fresh). **Load-bearing FP firewall: ONLY the positive-unification path returns non-null; union-checkType / different-target / arity-mismatch / non-infer-mismatch all return null → caller falls back to existing anyType behavior.** So the behavior change is confined to genuinely-related infer-conditionals (FP-safe; full-suite verified exactly one flip). Tuple/array/function-type infer positions + union-checkType distribution are NOT yet handled (forward extensions).
- **Primitive-resolving type-alias DISPLAY unfolds; object/interface alias keeps its name (B119)**: var-decl assignability errors normally render the target via `formatTypeForDisplay(typeAnnotation)` (the source-text alias name). But TypeScript UNFOLDS a type-alias that resolves to a PRIMITIVE intrinsic — `type N = number; let x: N = "s"` shows `'number'`, not `'N'`. `displayTargetAnnotation(typeAnnotation, targetType)` returns `typeToString(targetType)` when the annotation is a `TypeReference` to a `SymbolFlags.TypeAlias` AND `targetType is Type.Intrinsic` (excl. any/unknown/error); else `formatTypeForDisplay`. Currently wired only at the general `canUse && !isAssignable` TS2322 site (~56531) — if another var-decl emit site shows an alias name where TS shows the unfolded primitive, route it through this helper too.
- **`formatPropertyDisplayName` PRESERVES the source quote style of a non-identifier string-literal property name (B98.r118)**: a property whose name node is a `StringLiteralNode` and isn't a valid JS identifier renders with the ORIGINAL quote char — `{ '': number; }` for a single-quoted source name (`var A = { '': 3 }`), `{ "0": number; }` for a double-quoted one (`{ "0": 1 }`) — via `nameNode.singleQuote`. Do NOT hardcode one quote style: `typeOfOnTypeArg` needs single, `assignmentIndexedToPrimitives` needs double, and both are `.ts` (the `.tsx`-only double-quote-JSX cases aren't generated). A numeric-literal property name (`{ 0: 1 }`) is a `NumericLiteralNode`, not StringLiteralNode → renders unquoted `0`.
- **Tuple types use `Type.Object` with `tupleElementTypes` field**: `getTupleType` creates a `Type.Object` with numbered properties ("0", "1", ...), a `length` property with `NumberLiteral(n)` type, and `tupleElementTypes: List<Type>?` for display and identification. `typeToString` checks `tupleElementTypes` to display as `[T1, T2, ...]`.
- **Element access DISTRIBUTES over union receivers; TS2769 union-arg chains name the NULLISH member (B122)**: `getTypeOfElementAccess` delegates to `elementAccessResultType(objectType, indexExpr)` which, for a `Type.Union` receiver, maps each member through itself and `getUnionType`s the results — so `(number[] | null[])[0]` → `number | null` (the double element access `[[3,4],[null]][0][0]` was `anyType` before, masking the overload error in `arrayBestCommonTypes`). **Conservative gate (load-bearing):** the union result is produced ONLY when EVERY member yields a concrete (non-any/error) element type; any member resolving to `anyType` keeps the whole access `anyType` (preserves prior permissive behavior, bounds FP). PAIRED with the TS2769 overload-chain elaboration: `getUnionMemberFailureSubline` appends a third-level `Type 'undefined' is not assignable to type 'boolean'.` sub-line when the first failing arg is a `Type.Union` and the param is a `Type.Intrinsic` primitive — TypeScript reports the NULLISH failing member FIRST (`undefined`, then `null`), else the first failing member (the `[4,2,undefined][0]`→`number|undefined` vs `boolean` chains report `undefined` even though `number` also fails). Gated to union-arg-vs-primitive-param so object/union targets keep their own elaboration. The two pieces are independently net-zero (element-access alone doesn't flip arrayBestCommonTypes; the chain alone never sees the union arg) — both are required together.
- **Array-literal element-type inference dedupes STRUCTURALLY, but `getUnionType` does NOT (B98.r162)**: `getTypeOfArrayLiteral` collapses structurally-identical element types via `ts2403Identical(...) == Ts2403Cmp.IDENTICAL` (the old reference-identity `!in` missed two fresh-but-equal anonymous object literals, so `[{name,id},{name,id}]` became a bogus `{name,id} | {name,id}` element union — TypeScript never displays `T | T`). The downstream symptom of a duplicate-member union is SILENT: `checkMemberAccessMissing`'s local-fallback (`else`) branch does `if (exprType !is Type.Object) return`, so a `Type.Union` receiver (even an all-identical-members one) bails out of TS2339 entirely — whereas property-access-ON-a-union like `x.id` still resolves member-wise — which is what hid `lambdaParamTypes`' `x.foo`. **`getUnionType` (Checker.kt:~83926) still dedupes by `it.id` only**, so any union constructed from structurally-identical-but-distinct `Type.Object` instances keeps duplicates; adding `ts2403Identical` dedup there is the general fix but `getUnionType` is called everywhere (broad regression risk), so it was deliberately left scoped to the array-literal path. When a diagnostic mysteriously fails to fire on a value whose type "should" be a single object, check whether it's actually a duplicate-member `Type.Union`.
- **`getTypeFromTypeReference` errorType guard**: When creating `Type.Reference` from a TypeReference with type arguments, skip Reference creation if any resolved type argument is `errorType` (unresolved type parameter). Otherwise `C2<T>` displays as `C2<error>` instead of falling back to `C2<T>` display.
- **Variable initializer inference scope**: `currentLocalTypes` is populated from unannotated variable initializers (widened) during the TS2322 walk. Must skip `null`/`undefined`/`void` initializers to avoid FPs in "declare then assign" patterns. `getTypeFromTypeQuery` (typeof) must NOT use `currentLocalTypes` — function-scoped variables shouldn't be visible in type annotation positions.
- **Type subclasses are nested inside `sealed class Type`**: To avoid name conflicts with AST TypeNode subclasses (`UnionType`, `IntersectionType`, `TypeReference`, `TypeParameter` in Ast.kt), the checker's semantic type classes are nested: `Type.Intrinsic`, `Type.Union`, `Type.Intersection`, `Type.Object`, `Type.Interface`, `Type.Reference`, `Type.TypeParam`. Use `when (type) { is Type.Union -> ... }` etc.
- **`TypeFlags` companion shadows Kotlin type names**: `TypeFlags.String`, `TypeFlags.Number`, `TypeFlags.Boolean`, `TypeFlags.Object` shadow Kotlin types inside the `TypeFlags` companion. Outside the companion, `String` refers to `kotlin.String` as normal. Inside the companion, use `kotlin.String` if you need the Kotlin type.

- **Interface call/construct signatures are `MethodDeclaration` with special names**: The parser produces `MethodDeclaration(name=Identifier(""))` for call signatures and `MethodDeclaration(name=Identifier("new"))` for construct signatures in interfaces/type literals. `resolveInterfaceMembers` must detect these and add to `callSignatures`/`constructSignatures` lists, NOT as named properties. Otherwise they appear as property "" or "new" and cause FPs in TS2430 and structural comparison.
- **Call/construct signature resolution must push enclosing interface's `typeParameters` into scope**: in `resolveInterfaceMembers`'s call/construct sig branch, set `currentTypeParamScope` to include the interface's TPs (plus any sig-own TPs from `member.typeParameters`) BEFORE resolving return type and parameter type annotations. Pre-resolve param types into `symbolTypes[paramSym.id]` so later `getTypeOfSymbol(paramSym)` returns the in-scope-resolved type after scope restoration. Without this, `T` references in `interface I<T> { (a: T): T; }` resolve through `getTypeFromTypeReference` with null scope → fall to globals → `errorType` (cached in `nodeTypes` because `cacheable = currentTypeParamScope == null`). Downstream `instantiateSignature` calls become no-ops on errorType — silent failure, no diagnostic emitted. Same fix likely needed for any other site that resolves member type annotations from inside an interface/class declaration without pushing the type-param scope.
- **Class construct signatures are static-side only**: `objectTypeRelatedTo` must skip construct signature comparison for class/interface instance types (`isClassInstance` check). Construct signatures on classes belong to the static side (typeof Class), used for `new` expression checking. Comparing construct signatures during assignment causes FPs when source class has no explicit constructor but target does.
- **`getReturnTypeOfCallExpression` uses `sigs[0]` only**: No proper overload resolution. For named interfaces with multiple call signatures, returns `anyType` to avoid picking the wrong overload. Only resolves for single-signature or anonymous function types.
- **Full Object↔Object comparison blocked by recursive types**: Opening `canUseTypeEngine` for all Object↔Object causes 39+ regressions from infinite type expansion (e.g., `interface List<T> { next: List<T> }`). Safe subset: anonymous source → named Interface target. Named→named requires recursive cycle detection in structural comparison.
