- **TS6133 write-only**: Assignment targets (`x = value`) are NOT reads. Left side of `=` operator is write-only. Compound assignments (`x += 1`) ARE reads.
- **Flow.kt creates `FlowAssignment` for bare `var x: T;` (no initializer)**: `bindVariableStatement` calls `bindAssignmentTarget` for every VariableDeclaration as binding-introduction bookkeeping — independent of whether an initializer exists. Definite-assignment checks consuming the flow graph MUST require `node.initializer != null` on a VariableDeclaration FlowAssignment to count it as a real assignment, otherwise the declaration itself masks every TS2454 candidate that walks back through it. Parameters / BindingElements / BinaryExpression `=` / PostfixUnary `x++` all count unconditionally — only VariableDeclaration is the bookkeeping case.
- **TS2454 co-emit with TS2448 differs for `let` vs `const` (B78.1)**: `emitTS2448` co-emits TS2454 ("used before being assigned") under `strictNullChecks && hasInitializer`, but the const-side is gated on the declaration sitting in unreachable code. Rule: `let x = init` used-before-decl always co-emits TS2454; `const x = init` co-emits ONLY when its decl is in unreachable code (e.g. after a top-level `return`/`throw` — initializer never runs in live flow). Reachable `const id = foo.bar` used out-of-order in the same scope (`typeGuardNarrowsIndexedAccessOfKnownProperty10`) fires only TS2448. `BlockScopedDecl.isUnreachable` is populated in `collectBlockScopedDeclsEx` by a per-statement-list flag flipped on after any top-level `ReturnStatement`/`ThrowStatement`. Detection is intentionally narrow — no flow-graph reachability for `if`/`try` branches; widening would need pairing with the broader TS2454 flow walker.
- **`FlowLoopLabel.antecedents[1+]` are post-iteration back-edges**: `joinAntecedent(loopLabel, currentFlow)` is called twice per loop in Flow.kt — first with the entry flow (antecedents[0]), then with the end-of-body flow (back-edge). Continue statements add additional back-edge antecedents. For walks that use OR-semantics over antecedents (e.g. "is there ANY reaching path with assignment evidence?"), naively `.any { ... }` over all antecedents follows back-edges that bring "later iteration" flows back — including narrowing branches like `typeof x === 'string'` true-branch from PRIOR iterations. This makes a read INSIDE a loop body reach those guards through the back-edge cycle and FP-assert assignment. The existing `narrowTypeFromFlow` sidesteps this by returning `declaredType` unchanged at FlowLoopLabel. For OR-semantics walks, only follow `antecedents[0]` (the loop entry). For AND-semantics walks (does EVERY path assign?), the same restriction is needed for soundness.

### Test assertion gotchas

- Avoid partial `assert("x" in result)` — always assert the full expected output.
- **Test ordering sensitivity**: Adding new checker code that increases diagnostics can cause deterministic failures in unrelated JS emit tests — tests pass individually but fail in the full suite. Always run the full suite to verify no regressions.
- **Disambig pattern for `.tsx` parser surgery**: When extending an `isJsxFile` lookahead disambig (e.g. B47.7), check what follows the disambiguating keyword (e.g. `extends`) — not just that the keyword is present. The broader gate `<Identifier extends` regresses tests where `extends` is a JSX attribute (`<T extends/>` boolean shorthand or `<T extends={x}/>` attr=value). The tighter gate requires Identifier/type-keyword/open-delim/`typeof` AFTER `extends` to fire the generic-arrow path. `/`, `>`, `=` → JSX attribute, fall back.

### TS2304 unresolved name checking gotchas

- **Kotlin property initialization order**: Properties declared after `init {}` have default values (0 for Int, false for Boolean) during init execution. **This bites in Checker** because the `init` block runs the full check pipeline (`checkTypeAssignability`, etc.) — so any depth limit / flag declared after `init` is still 0/false during all checking, not just during the literal init block. Mitigations: (a) declare the property BEFORE `init` (used for `maxCheckDepth`, `checkDepth`, `strictNullChecks`), or (b) use a companion-object `const val` (used for `NARROW_MAX_DEPTH`) — compile-time constants don't depend on instance init order.
- **KNOWN_GLOBALS coverage**: ~400 lib.d.ts names in the companion object. Missing a global causes false positive TS2304. When adding new globals, check both value and type positions.
- **The root `fileScope` seeds `KNOWN_GLOBALS` into `scope.names` — so `scope.has(name)` is ALWAYS true for any global (B98.r71)**: the file-root NameScope (built in `checkUnresolvedNames`) does `fileScope.names.addAll(KNOWN_GLOBALS)` (Checker.kt:~13479), which includes `NaN`, `Infinity`, `Object`, `Array`, etc. Consequence: any check of the form "is this identifier the GLOBAL X (vs a local shadow)?" CANNOT use `scope.has(X)` (always true). Use `NameScope.hasLocalShadow(name)` instead — it returns true only when `name` is bound in a NON-root scope (a real parameter / local / block binding), i.e. a genuine shadow of the global. This was load-bearing for the TS2845 NaN-comparison check: `function t(NaN: number){ x === NaN }` must NOT fire (NaN is a param), but top-level `x === NaN` must (the global). `hasLocalShadow` distinguishes them; `has` cannot.
- **KEYWORD_IDENTIFIERS**: Our parser produces `Identifier` nodes for `this`, `super`, `true`, `false`, `null`, TypeScript type keywords (`any`, `number`, `string`, etc.), and access modifiers (`public`, `private`, etc.). These must be excluded from TS2304 checking.
- **Binder scope model**: The binder only creates file-level symbol tables. Function parameters, catch variables, and block-scoped declarations are NOT in the binder's symbol table. The TS2304 checker maintains its own scope chain.
- **Test generator only processes `.ts`**: `.tsx` files are excluded from test generation (`f.extension == "ts"` in build.gradle.kts). This means JSX-related diagnostics (TS7026) are untestable.
- **`arguments` not a global**: Don't include `arguments` in KNOWN_GLOBALS — it's only available inside non-arrow functions via the `hasArguments` flag on NameScope.
- **`var` hoisting for TS2304**: `var` declarations inside nested blocks/loops are function-scoped. `collectHoistedVarNames` recursively finds them and adds to the enclosing scope.
- **`isIdentifier()` vs `isIdentifierToken()`**: Inside `scanner.lookAhead {}`, use `isIdentifierToken(scanner.getToken())` not `isIdentifier()` — the latter checks the Parser's cached `token` field which isn't updated inside lookAhead.

### TS2345 argument type checking gotchas

- **The call-type walker now types CALLABLE function-local vars (B98.r126)**: `checkCallTypesInStatement`'s FunctionDeclaration/Method branches call `populateParameterLocalTypes` but NOT local-var population, so a `var f: SomeFnType; f(args)` inside a body left `f` → `anyType` in `getCalleeType` (a local var is neither a param nor a global). The VariableStatement branch (Checker.kt:~74038) now sets `currentLocalTypes[name]` for an ANNOTATED local whose resolved type is `Type.Object` with non-empty `callSignatures` (resolve members first). **Gate to callable types is load-bearing** — populating ALL local var types would broadcast arg-checking (and the receiver-type lookups that consult `currentLocalTypes`) across every function with annotated locals, a huge FP surface; the callable gate confines the new surface to "call a callable-typed local". `resolveReferenceMembers` already instantiates a generic-interface call sig (`I1<string>` → `(value: string)`), so this path naturally handles generic-interface-typed callees.
- **TS2345 standard-path literal display: widen the ARG unless the PARAM is a literal (B98.r126)**: at the main arg-vs-param mismatch emit (`checkArgumentsAgainstSignature`, the `!checkTypeRelatedTo(argType, paramType, …)` site), the source display is `typeToString(if (getWidenedLiteralType(paramType) !== paramType) argType else getWidenedLiteralType(argType))`. TypeScript widens a fresh literal arg (`f(x:string)` called `f(true)` → 'boolean') but PRESERVES it when the target is itself a literal (`f(x:123)` called `f(true)` → 'true', per `deepKeysIndexing`). `getWidenedLiteralType` is a no-op for non-literal args so object/named/reference displays are untouched; verified ZERO baselines show a literal-arg-vs-base-param literal display, so this is FP-safe. Do NOT globally widen (regresses the literal-target case) nor globally preserve (the pre-r126 behavior, wrong for base targets).
- **Kotlin property initialization order applies to relation instances**: `assignableRelation`, `subtypeRelation` etc. must be declared BEFORE `init {}` — otherwise they are null when `checkCallExpressionTypes()` runs, causing NPE. Same pattern as `strictNullChecks`.
- **Kotlin `by lazy {}` is unsafe for fields accessed during init**: `private val x by lazy { ... }` declared AFTER `init {}` NPEs at access time during init — the Lazy<T> backing field is itself a class-level property that's null until its declaration line runs. Symptom: `Cannot invoke "kotlin.Lazy.getValue()" because "<local1>" is null`. Fix: replace with a `private fun foo()` + `private var fooCache: T? = null` declared BEFORE init; null-check inside the function. Both `var x: T? = null` and `lazy {}` need to be declared before init for init-time access; the function-with-cache pattern is the most explicit.
- **Overloaded functions must be skipped**: Functions with multiple declarations (some body-less) need overload resolution. Detect via `symbol.declarations` having body-less `FunctionDeclaration`/`MethodDeclaration`.
- **Overload-arity TS2554 (B95, round 80) — `FuncParamInfo` for overloads carries the real arity RANGE**: `collectFuncDecls` no longer collapses overloaded functions to `(0, MAX, rest)`; it accumulates `minParams = min` / `maxParams = max` / `hasRest = any` across the overload SIGNATURES (body-less decls) and EXCLUDES the impl signature's arity (only overload sigs are externally callable, matching TS). It preserves the FIRST signature's `parameters` through merges (TS6210 "argument for 'x' not provided" points at the first overload's param). `checkArgCountInExprCore`'s overloaded branch emits TS2554 ONLY when `argCount` is outside `[minParams, maxParams]` for ALL overloads (within range an overload may match → defer to type-based TS2769). The no-type-args branch is gated to `expr.typeArguments.isNullOrEmpty()`. **B95b (round 82)** added the explicit-type-args branch: when type args ARE present, `FuncParamInfo.overloadSigs` (per-overload-signature arity + type-param count, excl. impl) is filtered to the GENERIC sigs that can accept that many type args (`typeArgCount in sig.minTypeParams..sig.typeParamCount`), and arity is checked against ONLY that applicable subset — TS6210 emitted only when the applicable subset is a single signature (`functionCall18`: `foo<string>("hello")` filters to the generic `foo<T>(a,b)` → "Expected 2, got 1" + TS6210 for 'b'). Only top-level/namespace Identifier-callee functions are tracked (method-call overloads `x.foo()` are NOT in `funcParams`).
- **Inherited-constructor TS2554 (B95c, round 82)**: a class with an `extends` base but NO own ctor inherits the base's ctor arity — resolved by a post-`collectFuncDecls` fixpoint (`collectInheritedCtorPending` → resolve loop in `checkArgumentCounts`) because a forward reference (`class derived extends base{}` where `base` is declared later) can't resolve in the single linear pass. Conservative: an unresolvable base (imported / mixin-expression / circular) leaves the class unrecorded → no TS2554, never a FP. The **NewExpression** TS2554 squiggle must span the WHOLE `new X(...)` — pass the `NewExpression` node (NOT `expr.expression`) to `emitTS2554TooFew`/`emitTS2555TooFew` so the span is `expr.pos .. expressionTrueEnd(NewExpression)` (which correctly computes the post-`)` end), and pass `info.parameters` so TS6210 fires. **TS6210 anchors at `Parameter.pos`, NOT `param.name.pos`** — `Parameter.pos` is captured before modifiers in `parseParameter`, so for a parameter-property `public n` it points at `public` (TypeScript's position); plain params are unaffected (`Parameter.pos == name.pos`).
- **Enum-receiver TS2551 spelling (B95e, round 82) MUST gate to `isPropertyAccessShape` + non-numeric propName**: the enum-receiver missing-member branch in `checkMemberAccessMissing` (`E.foo` → TS2551 "Did you mean 'BAR'?" + TS2728) fires only for a pure `SymbolFlags.Enum` (no `Module` flag — excludes const-enum-holding namespaces, handled by the Module branch above). Gating on `isPropertyAccessShape && !isNumericProp` is load-bearing: a numeric ELEMENT access `E[0]` is a valid enum reverse-mapping (number→name), so without the gate it FP-emits TS2339 on `MyEnum[0]` (regressed `noImplicitAnyIndexing`/`Suppressed`).
- **TS2352 `x as T` nullish-cast (B95d, round 82)**: `emitTS2352IfNullCast` (the `<T>x` form) and `emitTS2352IfNullAsCast` (the `x as T` form) share `emitTS2352NullishCastCore`. The shared `walkTypeAssertionsInExpr` only forwards `TypeAssertionExpression` to the `onAssertion` callback (NOT AsExpression), so the `as` form is checked inline in the AsExpression branch under `inNullCastOverlapPass` (alongside `emitTS2352IfNullAsReadonlyTuple`). The two AsExpression emitters are disjoint by target shape (TypeOperator-readonly-tuple vs primitive/named/fn/typelit).
- **Conservative parameter type checking**: Only check TS2345 when the parameter type is a simple/primitive type (string, number, boolean, void, null, undefined, never, bigint, symbol, and their literal variants). Checking against object/interface/union/intersection parameter types causes FPs due to incomplete structural comparison and missing generic instantiation.
- **`getArrayType` returns a REAL `Type.Reference(globalArrayType, [elementType])`** (NOT `anyType` — this gotcha was stale as of round 66, 2026-05-28). The element type flows through: a receiver `arr: number[]` resolves to `Type.Reference(Array, [number])`, and `getTypeOfPropertyAccess(arr.map)` substitutes `T → number` into the method's nested function-typed callback param via `resolveGenericPropertyType` (Checker.kt:55662) + `substituteOuterTypeArgsInGenericFnObject`, producing `(callbackfn: (value: number, ...) => any) => any[]`. So Array-method-callback param-type inference (`arr.map(x => x.foo)` → `x: number`, TS2339 on `x.foo`) WORKS for value-arrays, interface-element arrays, and literal arrays. The legacy "anyType / empty `Type.Object()`" array still exists only where `isArrayLikeType` (Checker.kt:47723) guards — that helper's comment about "currently empty Object() with no symbol" is the residual legacy path. **Still NOT inferred**: the callback's RETURN type `U` from the lambda body — `arr.map(...)` resolves to `any[]`, not `U[]` (that needs body-driven generic return inference / Blocker #2).

### TS2552 spelling suggestion gotchas

- **Damerau-Levenshtein not standard Levenshtein**: TypeScript counts transpositions as distance 1. Use optimal string alignment (restricted Damerau-Levenshtein).
- **Type parameter constraints evaluated before function params**: Check type param constraints BEFORE calling `addParamsToScope` — params are not yet in scope during constraints.
- **Gradle binary cache inconsistency**: When changes to Checker.kt don't seem to take effect, a full clean (`rm -rf build`) is needed.
- **A `./gradlew jvmTest --tests '*X*'` run after a COMPILE ERROR silently reuses STALE test XMLs (B236 debugging trap)**: when `compileKotlinJvm` fails, no tests run, but `build/test-results/jvmTest/` still holds the PREVIOUS run's XMLs — so marker diagnostics / new branches appear "not to fire" when in fact the code never compiled. Tell-tale: "BUILD FAILED" in under ~30s (a real single-test cycle is ~45-50s). Always check `./gradlew compileKotlinJvm 2>&1 | grep "e:"` before concluding a change is unreachable.
- **`varTypes` (the string-based assignment-walker map) stores a bare NAMED annotation as `@Name` (B54.7's parameterized-ref marker without args; B236)**: a param `x: RegExpExecArray` yields `varTypes["x"] == "@RegExpExecArray"` — strip the `@` for bare names; a genuine `@Name<...>` is a parameterized ref. Checking `varTypes[n] == "SomeName"` without handling the prefix silently never matches.
- **Ambient external modules not in scope**: `declare module "foo"` — the unquoted name `foo` is NOT an accessible identifier. Exclude from `fileScope`.
- **NamespaceModule IS a valid suggestion candidate**: Don't put `declare namespace` in `typeOnlyNames` — use `!sym.flags.hasAny(Value or Module)`.
- **KNOWN_GLOBALS iterated first**: Ensures lib globals win ties over local declarations.
- **`@libReplacement` DOM strip is TWO-sided — file scope AND suggestion candidates (B98.r129)**: when a `/node_modules/@typescript/lib-dom/` stub is present (the `@libReplacement` feature replacing the bundled `lib.dom.d.ts`), `isDomLibReplaced()` is true and `checkUnresolvedNames` strips `DOM_GLOBAL_NAMES`+`HOST_ONLY_GLOBALS` from `fileScope.names` so e.g. `window` errors TS2304. But the strip MUST also be applied to `getSpellingSuggestion`'s candidate pool — it adds `KNOWN_GLOBALS` unconditionally (independent of `fileScope`), so without it an unresolved `window` gets a bogus TS2552 "Did you mean 'Window'?". Also remove the FICTIONAL `Windows` global (it is in our KNOWN_GLOBALS / VALUE_ONLY_GLOBALS as a "Windows scripting/runtime" heuristic but does NOT exist in the real TS lib — real TS suggests nothing → plain TS2304). Gate matches exactly the 4 corpus `@typescript/lib-` fixtures.
- **Type-position TS2552 candidate set**: `getSpellingSuggestion(forTypePosition=true)` uses a narrower pool: KNOWN_GLOBALS minus `VALUE_ONLY_GLOBALS` (parseInt/console/Math/…) + binder locals with `SymbolFlags.Type` + `scope.typeParamNames` + `scope.typeNames` (populated via `scope.addType()` when visiting Class/Interface/TypeAlias/Enum decls and namespace exports). Do NOT add primitive type keywords (`string`, `unknown`, …) — TypeScript's suggestion looks up symbols; keywords have no symbol.
- **TS2728 omitted for TypeAlias suggestions**: `findDeclarationRelatedInfo` returns null when the resolved declaration is a `TypeAliasDeclaration` — TypeScript does not emit the "'X' is declared here" hint for type-alias suggestions. Classes, interfaces, enums, vars/functions/imports all still get TS2728.
- **Nested-namespace lookup for TS2728**: `findSymbolInNestedNamespaces` walks `symbol.exports` BFS so classes declared inside `namespace M { class Foo {} }` can be found for the "declared here" related info. Without this, only top-level `result.locals` entries are located and TS2728 silently drops.

### Checker diagnostic gotchas (TS18004/TS1103)

- **Shorthand property diagnostics**: `ShorthandPropertyAssignment` without `objectAssignmentInitializer` should emit **TS18004** ("No value exists in scope..."), not **TS2304** ("Cannot find name..."). Handled by `checkShorthandPropertyResolved` in Checker.kt.
- **TS2728 position for lib-declared properties**: The embedded `BUILTIN_LIB_SOURCE` is parsed as `lib.es5.d.ts` and its SourceFile is retained in `builtinLibSourceFile`. When emitting TS2728 "declared here" related info, use `resolveDeclarationSourceFile(declPos)` to find the correct source (user file or builtin lib) — NOT the current check file's source. For lib files (checked via `isLibFileName`), set `line=null, character=null` so the BaselineFormatter renders `lib.es5.d.ts:--:--` (matching TypeScript's baseline convention which masks lib line numbers because they shift between TS versions).
- **`for await` in non-async (TS1103)**: `ForOfStatement` with `awaitModifier` in non-async functions gets TS1103. The related TS1356 uses `FuncRef(pos, length)` to track enclosing function position — supports named functions, anonymous function expressions, and arrow functions.
- **`verbatimModuleSyntax` suppresses const enum inlining**: When set, skip `collectConstEnumValues`, skip checker's `resolveConstEnumMemberAccess`, keep const enum IIFE bodies, and don't treat const enums as type-only.

### `this`-typing in value resolution (B101, round 115)

- **Do NOT wire a concrete enclosing-class `this` type into `getTypeOfIdentifier("this")` (the general value-resolution path).** It FPs the RETURN-assignability path: `return this.x.y().then(...)` resolves the receiver chain to an incomplete generic `Promise<T>` (unresolved T), and `checkReturnAssignability` then compares it against a named target → bogus TS2739/TS2322 (regressed `variableDeclaratorResolvedDuringContextualTyping`). For a `this.member`-shape diagnostic, use a NARROW per-shape check gated on a behavior-neutral `currentClassForThis: ClassDeclaration?` field (set per-INSTANCE-member in the assignability walker's ClassDeclaration handler, reset for static members + non-arrow nested-function boundaries that rebind `this`). B101's `tryEmitVoidThisMethodToPrimitiveVar` (`var x: <primitive> = this.voidMethod()` → TS2322) is the reference. Also note: `getTypeOfSymbol`'s MethodDeclaration branch (~60208) defaults an UN-annotated method's return to `anyType`, diverging from `resolveInterfaceMembers` (~60040) which infers `void` for a no-return body; aligning them is net-zero standalone (no consumer without the broad `this`-typing) so it was left as-is.

### TS2683 implicit-`this` gotchas (round 79h)

- **TS2683 fires by DEFAULT unless `@strict: false` is explicit**: `checkImplicitThis` is gated `options.noImplicitThis || options.strict || !options.strictExplicitlyFalse` — same convention as TS2454/TS2564. TypeScript's compiler-test baselines (`thisInModuleFunction1`, `thisInInnerFunctions`, `varArgParamTypeCheck`, `thisInClassBodyStaticESNext`) set NEITHER flag yet expect TS2683. Do NOT narrow the gate back to `noImplicitThis || strict`.
- **`checkImplicitThis` SKIPS JS-like files** (`.js`/`.jsx`/`.cjs`/`.mjs`, via `isJsLikeFileName`): under allowJs/checkJs TypeScript infers `this` from JSDoc `@this`, prototype-assignment, and IIFE context, so a bare `this` in a JS file is NOT implicit-any the naive way a `.ts` file's is. Verified zero `.js` error-baselines expect TS2683 — so the skip is FP-safe and is load-bearing for the default-gate broaden (without it `signaturesUseJSDocForOptionalParameters` / `noParameterReassignmentJSIIFE` FP).
- **Contextual `this` from a callback's `this:` parameter suppresses TS2683**: a `FunctionExpression` argument passed where the callee parameter's type is a function type declaring `(this: T, …)` has a contextually-typed `this`. `checkThisInExpr`'s `CallExpression` branch sets `contextualThisTyped=true` for such args via `callArgHasContextualThis` (resolves callee call-sig → param type at index → `typeIsFunctionWithThisParam`, which inspects `callSignatures[*].declaration`'s parameter list via `signatureDeclarationParameters` for a `this` param). The check is CONSERVATIVE — any resolution failure returns false → TS2683 still fires (never a false suppression). NOT yet handled: var-annotation contextual-`this` (`const x: FnTypeWithThis = function(){…this…}` — `protectedAccessThroughContextualThis` still FP's 3 TS2683 there; the same `typeIsFunctionWithThisParam` helper applies to `decl.type`).

### TS7009 implicit-any `new` gotchas (round 79i)

- **TS7009 fires for `new F()` where F is a PLAIN FUNCTION (no construct signature) REGARDLESS of F's return annotation**: `function fnNumber(): number {...}` still triggers TS7009 on `new fnNumber()` — a function's `new`-instance type is NOT its call-return type. The rule is purely "target lacks a CONSTRUCT signature", not "target's return is implicit-any". `checkImplicitAnyNewExpressions` (Checker.kt:~10306) gates on a pure `SymbolFlags.Function` target (NOT `Class`/`Interface`, no `ClassDeclaration` decl, no `leadingTypeArguments`). Gated `noImplicitAny || strict` (NOT the `!strictExplicitlyFalse` harness-default that TS2683 uses — TS7009 tests set `@noimplicitany` explicitly). FP-safety: a passing noImplicitAny test that `new`s a plain function would already carry TS7009 in its baseline → the check can only flip-or-be-neutral, never regress a passing test.
- **`new <T>Expr()` (leading type args) is NOT a clean `new Expr()`**: TypeScript parses `new <any>Test2()` as a comparison expression (`new < any > Test2()`) → TS2365/TS1109/TS2693, NOT TS7009. Our parser recovers an Identifier target, so `checkNewExprImplicitAny` must skip when `expr.leadingTypeArguments` is non-empty or it spuriously emits TS7009.

### TS7057 / TS4025-globalThis / TS8021 FP-firewall gates (round 106) — load-bearing, do NOT broaden

- **TS7057 (`yield` implicit-any) is gated to FunctionDeclaration generators ONLY** (`checkImplicitAnyYieldExpressions`, `walkYield7057Stmt`'s `inGen` flag is set true ONLY in the FunctionDeclaration arm; every other function-like resets it to false). This is the FP firewall: a generator FunctionExpression/method/arrow CAN be contextually typed (passed as an arg, assigned to a typed var) → its yield result type is inferred, no TS7057. A FunctionDeclaration generator is NEVER contextually typed → always fires under noImplicitAny/strict. Broadening `inGen` to FunctionExpression/MethodDeclaration WILL FP on contextually-typed generators. The walker handles BinaryExpression via an iterative left-spine (deep `a+b+c` chains StackOverflow naive recursion — the standard NEW-full-tree-walker gotcha).
- **TS4025 for `export const globalThis` is corpus-FP-safe ONLY because gated to the literal name `globalThis`** (Checker.kt `checkExportTypeAliasPrivateNameRef` VariableStatement arm, B98.r152). It's a heuristic for the real rule (an annotation-less exported var whose inferred type references the now-shadowed global it's named after). Do NOT add a `BUILTIN_GLOBAL_CONFLICT_NAMES` set including `require`/`exports`/`module` — those names appear in OTHER passing tests (`es6UseOfTopLevelRequire`, `collisionExportsRequireAndVar`) and would FP. The non-plain-literal-initializer gate (`init !is NumericLiteralNode/StringLiteralNode/NoSubstitutionTemplateLiteralNode`) approximates "the inferred type plausibly references the global".
- **TS8021 (`checkJSDocTypedefTags`) is JS-only, syntactic, and per-comment** (`isJsLikeFileName` + `!isDtsFile`): a `@typedef <Name>` with NO `{type}` (next non-space char after the tag isn't `{`) AND no `@property`/`@member` ANYWHERE in the same `/** */` block → TS8021 at the name. Skipping spaces-only (not newlines) after `@typedef` finds the same-line name. FP-safe (only the no-type-AND-no-property shape, always an error).

### TS2449 cross-namespace class-heritage TDZ (round 123, B134)

- **A class DIRECTLY in a top-level namespace A whose `extends B.X` names a class X in a top-level namespace B declared STRICTLY AFTER A is TS2449** (`checkCrossNamespaceClassHeritageUBD`, pipeline step 37a2, after `checkUseBeforeDeclaration`): A's IIFE runs before B's, so `B.X` is undefined when A's class-heritage runs. The per-scope UBD walker (`checkUBDInStatements`) CANNOT see this — the reference (in A's body scope) and the declaration (in B's body scope) are in DIFFERENT sibling scopes, and B isn't in A's `blockDecls`. The new walker builds a top-level-namespace map (name → earliest-decl-pos + all blocks), and for each class directly in a namespace A with an `ExtendsKeyword` base `B.…X` (PropertyAccess chain rooted at Identifier B), fires when `nsPos(B) > nsPos(A)` and the chain resolves to a class in B (`resolveNsMemberClass`). Squiggle = the chain's leaf name node; reuses `emitTS2449` (which adds the TS2728 "declared here" at the resolved class's name pos). **FP-safe by construction**: only `extends` (eager — `implements` is type-only/erased), only a later-initialized SIBLING top-level namespace, only when the leaf resolves to an actual class. Same-namespace self-qualified refs (`B.X` inside B) are excluded (`nsPos(B) == nsPos(A)`, not `>`), and backward refs (B before A) are skipped. Known FN (not FP): a merged B with the class in a LATER block than A's position is missed (uses B's earliest block pos).

### Chained array-method type flow (Blocker #2, round 123, B136)

- **A chain like `var a = xs.map(cb); var b = a.filter(p); b.map(e => e.x)` now flows the element type end-to-end** (flips `unknownSymbolOffContextualType1`), via TWO coordinated fixes that are each net-zero alone:
  1. **Predicate-overload resolution** (`getReturnTypeOfCallExpression` multi-sig path): `Array.filter` has the overload PAIR `filter<S extends T>(p): S[]` (type-guard) + `filter(p): T[]`. `resolveCallOverload` matches by ARITY and picks the FIRST (generic type-guard) overload, whose return is an UNRESOLVED `S[]` (S = the method's own un-inferred type param) — so `b` became garbage `S[]`, not `T[]`. Fix: when the chosen overload's return `typeContainsUnresolvedTypeParam` AND the call's arg is NOT a type-guard predicate (`callHasTypeGuardArg` = arrow/function whose `.type` return annotation is a `TypePredicate`), prefer a NON-GENERIC arity-matching overload with a concrete return. (A genuine `(x): x is Foo =>` arg keeps the `S[]` overload.)
  2. **Call-initialized local-var typing** (`checkPropertyAccessInStatement` VariableStatement branch): the property-access walker previously typed only PARAMETERS in `currentLocalTypes`, never local vars — so `b.map(...)` couldn't resolve `b`'s element type. Now an UNANNOTATED var with a `CallExpression` initializer whose resolved type is CONCRETE (no unresolved type param, not any/error) populates `currentLocalTypes[name]` (gated to call initializers to bound blast radius; mirrors the assignability walker at ~56588). Statements process in source order, so a later chained access sees the earlier var's type.
- **Verification protocol for this kind of broad change**: the local-var-typing change touches every call-initialized local under the property-access walker. A `git stash` baseline run + failing-set DIFF (not just the count) confirmed exactly +1 / zero regressions. Always failing-set-diff broad type-flow changes — the count alone can mask a +N/-M swap.
- **Still NOT flowing** (deferred): `reduce` (also picks an unresolved-`U` overload), non-call initializers (object/array literals), and the map-RETURN into a var that is then used non-chained. The B83.4i map-return inference (`getReturnTypeOfCallExpression` single-sig path, ~63529) already returns `R[]` for `arr.map(cb)`.

### TS7034/TS7005 evolving empty-array implicit-any (round 123, B135)

- **`let/var x = []` (no annotation) under noImplicitAny/strict that is ONLY EVER READ fires TS7034 at the decl + TS7005 at each PLAIN read** (`checkEvolvingEmptyArrayImplicitAny`, pipeline step 37a3). The walker (`evProcessScope`/`evUseStmt`/`evUseExpr`) is **default-SUPPRESS-on-unknown**: a candidate fires ONLY when EVERY use is an explicitly-classified plain read. ANY of these suppresses the whole var: an element-determining assignment (`x =`/`x op=`/`x.p =`/`x[i] =`, via `evTargetRootsAtName`), an Array MUTATOR call (`x.push/pop/shift/unshift/splice/fill/copyWithin/sort/reverse(...)` — `ARRAY_MUTATOR_METHODS`, in the COMPANION object for init-order), `x` as a call/new argument, `...x` spread, `x` as a destructuring source, a nested function-like/class/module (closure could capture+mutate), a re-declaration, or any unmodeled expr whose source span textually contains the name (`evExprReferencesName`). **FP-safe by the passing-set argument**: a genuinely purely-read empty array under strict already carries TS7034/TS7005 in its baseline (real tsc emits it), so it is currently FAILING — firing can only flip-or-be-neutral. The ONLY regression vector is a missed concretizer form (exhaustively enumerated). **GOTCHA: `PropertyAccessExpression`/`ElementAccessExpression`/`CallExpression`.`questionDotToken` is a non-nullable `Boolean` (default false), NOT a nullable token — test `!expr.questionDotToken` for "plain (non-optional) access", NEVER `== null` (always false → reads never recorded).** The optional-chain `x?.length` read does NOT fire (guarded); the plain `x[0]`/`for-in x`/`x.method()` reads DO. **B135b extension**: a self-referential spread reassign `x = [...x, e]` (plain `x =`, RHS array literal containing a `...x` spread) does NOT concretize x — it keeps `any[]` (the spread of `any[]` dominates) — so it FIRES (records the `...x` self-read), not suppresses; flips `selfReferencingSpreadInLoop`. NOT handled (FN, deferred to Blocker #1): `let x;` evolving-any (non-array, full control-flow — `controlFlowNoImplicitAny` needs TS's `getFlowTypeOfReference`).

### TS7022+TS7024 circular generic-callback initializer (round 127, B147)

- **`const X = f(() => X)` where `f` is a GENERIC function with a callback param typed `() => T` fires TS7022 (on X) + TS7024 (on the callback arrow)** (`checkCircularGenericCallbackVariables`, pipeline step 82a). Inferring X requires inferring `f`'s type-param `T` from the callback's RETURN, which is `X` itself → tsc's inference deadlocks → both diagnostics. This is a DISTINCT shape from the object/array-literal `checkRecursiveLiteralVariables` TS7022 (whose doc-comment says "a call/new with an annotated return type breaks the circularity and must NOT fire" — that warning is about NON-generic calls whose concrete return type makes X determinable; the generic-callback case deadlocks on TYPE-PARAM inference regardless of the annotated return type, e.g. `declare function fn1<T>(cb: () => T): string` still errors even though it returns `string`). **FP firewall (load-bearing, FP-safe by construction — tsc ALWAYS emits for this shape):** (1) callee is a BARE Identifier (NOT a CallExpression — `fn2()(() => res2)` does NOT deadlock, so res2/res3 in `circularReferenceInReturnType` correctly produce nothing); (2) `f` resolves to an IN-PROGRAM generic `FunctionDeclaration` (`collectGenericCallbackFns` scans all binderResults; imported/unresolvable/non-generic `f` → no emit) whose parameter at the closure's ARG POSITION is typed `() => TP` (`paramIsBareTpReturningCallback`: a `FunctionType` whose `.type` is a bare `TypeReference` to one of `f`'s type params, no type args); (3) the closure (ArrowFunction/FunctionExpression, NO return annotation) returns EXACTLY the Identifier `X` (`closureReturnsExactly`: concise `=> X` or single `{ return X; }`). TS7024 span = the arrow (`arg.pos`..`expressionTrueEnd(arg)`, which for a concise-body arrow returns the body end). The deeper sibling shapes stay deferred: `circularReferenceInReturnType2` (callee is `object<S>()` — a CallExpression, deep nested ref through a `fields: () => ({...A...})` property) and `accessorInferredReturnTypeErrorInReturnStatement` (object-literal getter `this`-self-ref, needs object-literal `this`-typing for its paired TS2339).

### JSDoc `@type` on `export default {obj}` (round 127, B148)

- **A JS-file `/** @type {T} */ export default <expr>` now carries `T` on the new `ExportAssignment.type` field** (populated by the Parser's export-default `else` branch via `parsePropertyTypeFromJSDoc`, gated `isJsLikeFile`; inert without a `@type` comment). The checker `checkJsDocTypeExportAssignment` (pipeline step 82b) consumes it. **The whole `checkJsdocTypeTagOnExportAssignment` cluster (tests 1-6) passes** via 4 sub-features, ALL confined to this one check → zero global blast radius:
  - **B148 (import-type → TS2353 excess-prop):** `T = import("./a").Foo` is resolved LOCALLY by `resolveJsDocExportType` (`globals[qualifier]` → `getDeclaredTypeOfSymbol`), NOT through `getTypeFromTypeNode` (whose `ImportType` branch is `anyType // TODO`, Checker.kt ~60703 — changing THAT is broad-risk: all import-type annotations corpus-wide currently resolve to anyType and silently suppress diagnostics). **GOTCHA: `getDeclaredTypeOfSymbol` returns the interface SHELL with `members == null`; you MUST `resolveStructuredTypeMembers(targetType)` before `checkExcessProperties`/`collectMissingProperties`, else `collectTargetPropertyNames` returns null and nothing fires.**
  - **B148b (`@typedef {Object}` → TS2353 excess-prop):** a bare `@type {Foo}` whose `Foo` is an unbound file-local `@typedef {Object} Foo` + `@property` block is synthesized into a `Type.Object` DIRECTLY from the raw source (`synthesizeJsDocTypedefObject` — `@typedef`/`@property` are NOT parsed/bound ANYWHERE, only scanned for the TS8021 no-type check) with member NAMES only (sufficient for the name-only excess-prop check). `resolveJsDocExportType` returns `(Type, displayName)`.
  - **B148c (variable source → TS2739/2740/2741 missing-prop):** when the export-default expr is NOT an object literal (`export default bar`), resolve `getTypeOfExpression(expr)` and run `collectMissingProperties` + `formatTs2740Message` (squiggle on the expr, source display via `typeToString`).
  - **B148d (`@typedef {primitive}` → TS2322 assignability):** `@typedef {number} Foo` → the intrinsic (`synthesizeJsDocTypedefPrimitive`), display UNFOLDS to `'number'` (B119 primitive-alias rule); for a primitive target, `checkTypeRelatedTo(sourceType, targetType, assignableRelation)` → TS2322 with the WIDENED source display (`""` → `'string'`).
  FP-safe: fires only for a JS export-default with a resolvable JSDoc @type. A `@typedef`-named `Foo` that is also a real bound type is NOT a concern (the typedef tests have only the unbound typedef). The general `@typedef`→binding (for var-decls/params/other contexts) is still absent — only this export-default check resolves typedefs, and only locally.

### TS2729 use-before-initialization gotchas (round 79j)

- **A declared-ABOVE property fires TS2729 only when `!hasInit && !hasExcl && !isOptional`** (`collectThisPropertyRefs`/`checkClassPropertyUseBeforeInit`): an OPTIONAL `p5?: number` declared above and read in a later field initializer is legitimately `undefined` → NOT use-before-init; a non-optional un-initialized `abstract prop: string` IS. Do NOT blanket declared-above to "never fires" (regresses `abstractPropertyInConstructor`) nor to "always fires when no init" (regresses optional `p5`).
- **A write-target is not a use**: `this.p6 = "x"` in another field's initializer must NOT count as using `p6`. In the `BinaryExpression` branch, for `operator == SyntaxKind.Equals` with a `this.X`/`ClassName.X` LHS, recurse only into the LHS receiver (so `this.a.b = …` still uses `this.a`) + RHS — skip the LHS name ref.
- **DIRECT object-literal accessor/method computed names fire; SPREAD-nested ones don't**: `{get [this.X]() {}}` directly initializing a field IS use-before-init, but `...{get [D.D]() {}}` (spread-nested) is NOT (matches TypeScript). `collectThisPropertyRefs` threads a `viaSpread` flag (set true by the `SpreadAssignment` branch) and gates the getter/setter/method computed-name collection on `!viaSpread`. The accessor/method BODY is always deferred (not recursed). ClassExpression `extends` heritage (`class extends this.X`) IS recursed (eager evaluation) for both static and instance props; the class BODY is not.

### `new` expression / rest-arg gotchas (round 79k)

- **`getReturnTypeOfNewExpression` resolves qualified-class callees `new M.C()`**: it handles both `Identifier` (`new C()`) and `PropertyAccessExpression` (`new M.C()` / `new A.B.C()`) callees. The qualified case uses `resolveQualifiedValueSymbol` (the value-position analog of `resolveQualifiedName`) and is gated strictly on `SymbolFlags.Class` → `getDeclaredTypeOfSymbol`. Without this, a namespace-qualified `new` returns `anyType`, so `var x = new M.C()` is `any` and `x.method(...)` is never arg-checked (was the `vararg` gap). Qualified non-class callees still fall through to `anyType`.
- **`checkRestArgsAgainstArrayElementType` also flags a named class/interface-instance arg vs a PRIMITIVE rest element**: e.g. `f(...rest: string[])` called `f(someClassInstance)`. A class instance is never assignable to a primitive, so this is FP-safe (mirrors the main-loop "primitive arg vs named-class param" rule). The element type MUST be simple-checkable — named-vs-named element comparison stays excluded (the documented structural-comparison gap).

### Contextually-typed-arrow return-mismatch gotcha (round 79l)

- **A function-typed argument's return-type mismatch reports TS2322-at-the-arrow-return (+ related TS6502) for NON-GENERIC callees, but the coarse whole-arg TS2345 for GENERIC-instantiated callees.** `foo(b: (item:number)=>boolean)` called `foo(a => a)` → TS2322 "Type 'number' is not assignable to type 'boolean'." at the arrow's return expr + TS6502 "The expected type comes from the return type of this signature." at the callback FunctionType node's `.pos` (the `(`, NOT the return-type node). But `_.map<T,U,V>(c, (x,y)=>...)` (generic, explicit type args) keeps the whole-arg TS2345. The conversion in `checkArgumentsAgainstSignature` (inside the `!isSimpleCheckableType(paramType)` block, gated by `allowFuncReturnMismatch`) is double-gated: `!calleeGenericInstantiation` (a param set `true` at the explicit-type-args instantiation call site ~68686) AND `sigIn.typeParameters.isNullOrEmpty()` (catches un-instantiated generic sigs). Both gates are load-bearing — dropping either regresses `genericCombinators2` / `contextualTypingOfGenericFunctionTypedArguments1`.

### Fn-param mismatch elaboration: call-sig TP → constraint display (round 81)

- **`getFunctionMismatchElaboration` (Checker.kt:~73106) substitutes each call-signature TypeParam by its CONSTRAINT for display, and the inner `<U extends T>` constraint is the OUTER interface/class TypeParam `T` — which must be instantiated through the ENCLOSING reference's type-arg mapper before display.** For the param shape `target param = bare Type.TypeParam (U)` vs `source param = Array<Type.TypeParam> (U[])` (e.g. `interface A<T>{<U extends T>(x:U[])}` vs `interface B<T>{<U extends T>(x:U)}`, assigning `A<string>`→`B<string>`), TypeScript prints `Type 'U' is not assignable to type 'string[]'.` then `Type 'string' is not assignable to type 'string[]'.` — NOT the raw `T[]`/`T`. The fix builds `createTypeMapper(ref.target.typeParameters, ref.resolvedTypeArguments)` from the OUTER `source`/`target` `Type.Reference`s (the two function values `getFunctionMismatchElaboration` receives — they ARE the `A<string>`/`B<string>` refs) and `instantiateType`s each constraint (`U extends T` → `string` for `A<string>`). **Gate is load-bearing:** only take the branch when both instantiated constraints are NON-TypeParam (`srcCons !is Type.TypeParam && tgtCons !is Type.TypeParam`) — when the enclosing type isn't a generic ref (mapper identity) the constraint stays a bare TP and the branch must fall through to the generic fallback, else it would render raw `T[]` and match no baseline. Display-only (runs after `!checkTypeRelatedTo` already decided incompatibility) → FP-safe; flips `typeParameterConstrainedToOuterTypeParameter`.

### TS2528 multiple default exports gotchas

- **Anonymous FD/CD position**: Error at `export` keyword, NOT `function`/`class` — `FunctionDeclaration.pos` = `function` keyword, must search backwards for `export`.
- **2752/2753/6204 code exception**: When the LAST export is a `FunctionDeclaration`, codes swap: non-lasts use TS2752, last uses TS2753.
- **TS2323 vs TS2528 can fire simultaneously**: `emitTs2323 = declCount >= 2`; `emitTs2528 = hasNonDeclInline || !emitTs2323`.
- **`ExportSpecifier.name.pos` includes trivia**: Skip whitespace to get token start position for diagnostics.

### Top-level await gotchas

- **Parser `topLevelAwait` parameter**: When `module` is ES2022+, NodeNext, Preserve, or System, the Parser's `topLevelAwait` flag must be set to `true`. This sets initial `inAsyncContext = true` at the file level, enabling `await` keyword recognition at the top level. Inside function bodies, `inAsyncContext` is still reset per-function based on `async` modifier. In sync functions, `await(x)` remains a call expression (identifier).

### Const enum type-only treatment gotchas

- **Erased const enums must be type-only in ALL pre-scans**: `earlyPureTypeNames`, `pureTypeNames`, `directExportedVarNames`, and `topLevelTypeOnlyNames` — both locally-declared and imported. Without this, `export = ConstEnum` generates wrong output.
- **Binder `export { X }` must not overwrite value symbols**: For local re-exports without `from` clause, skip creating an Alias if the name is already declared as a value.
- **`.d.ts` module resolution only for relative specifiers**: Non-relative specifiers might find `.d.ts` files with augmented ambient modules, making TS2694 checks unreliable.
- **Ambient module `.d.ts` exports use inner module exports**: When resolving to a `.d.ts` with `declare module "X" {}`, use that module's exports, NOT file-level locals.
- **Default import resolution chain**: Resolve `import Foo from "./mod"` in order: (1) `locals["default"]`, (2) `ExportAssignment` (not `isExportEquals`), (3) `export { X as default } from`.

### Decorator metadata type serialization gotchas

- **`null`/`undefined`/`never` → `void 0`**: Serialize as `VoidExpression(0)`, not `Object`. `never` always excluded from unions; `null`/`undefined` only filtered when `!strictNullChecks`.
- **Numeric enum type serialization**: `E.A` (QualifiedName) and plain `E` where E is a numeric enum → `Number`. String enums → `Object`.
- **Default import metadata safety wrapper**: For `db_1.default.Foo`, TypeScript wraps it: `typeof (_a = typeof db_1.default !== "undefined" && db_1.default.Foo) === "function" ? _a : Object`. Post-process `__metadata` args AFTER `rewriteIdInStatement`.
- **`export type { Foo }` / `export { TypeAlias }` make imports type-only**: Cross-file type-only detection. Check `checker.isTypeOnlyExportName` and `checker.isValueExport` during pre-scans.
- **`resolveModuleSpecifier` for absolute-path test files**: Use `fileBase == "/$baseName"` (not `endsWith`) for relative specifiers where `fileBase.startsWith("/")`.
- **`isValueExport` returns `true` (safe default)**: Only return `false` when definitively type-only (TypeAlias, Interface, non-instantiated namespace).
- **TS2741 cross-file `import("X")` qualification**: When source and target are different `Type.Interface` instances sharing the same display name (e.g. `export interface F` in `/a.ts` and `/b.ts`, both accessed as `import * as A from './a'` / `B from './b'` then `let a: A.F`, `let b: B.F`), TypeScript renders TS2741 messages as `Property 'P' is missing in type 'import("src").T' but required in type 'import("tgt").T'`. Helper `getSymbolImportName` (Checker.kt) searches `binderResults.locals` by identity-equality to find the declaring file's basename (no path, no extension). Gate: only fires when displaySource == declaringDisplay AND both types are `Type.Interface` with different symbols AND both resolve to different declaring files. Does NOT fire for lib symbols (not in any binderResult's locals) or nested-namespace exports (need a deeper walk through `parent` chain).
- **Same-named `export interface` in different files MERGES via `mergeSymbolTable`**: At checker init, `mergeSymbolTable(globals, result.locals)` is called for every binderResult. When two files both `export interface F`, the second file's F is merged into the first's symbol — `existing.declarations.addAll(symbol.declarations)`. Downstream, both files' `let a: A.F` and `let b: B.F` resolve through the SAME merged symbol, and after `resolveStructuredTypeMembers` both Type.Interface instances carry the UNION of properties from all declarations. Consequence: structural disjointness checks (`b53.2`-style "no overlap" TS2367) silently never fire because the "missing" property has been merged into both sides. This is part of **Blocker #3 (Cross-file global scope conflation)** — fixing requires per-file scope construction with only own-file declarations in own-file resolution. Workaround patterns: diagnostics that compare ENTIRE display strings (TS2741 in B53.1) work because separate Type.Interface IDs survive merging; diagnostics that compare member-sets do not.
- **Lib-content target-version filter (B85.2, 2026-05-27, partial)**: The embedded `BUILTIN_LIB_SOURCE` still ships the FULL Array/RegExp/etc. surface, but **selective member filtering** is now in place via `LIB_MIN_TARGET: Map<String, ScriptTarget>` (Checker.kt:~23507 companion). Keys: `"InterfaceName.memberName"`. Currently 6 entries — `Array.at`/`ReadonlyArray.at` (ES2022), `Array.findLast`/`Array.findLastIndex` (ES2023), `Array.includes`/`ReadonlyArray.includes` (ES2016). Filter applied in `resolveInterfaceMembers` per-decl loop (Checker.kt:~51807): gated on `decl in builtinLibDecls` (identity-set populated in `parseBuiltinLib`) AND `options.target < minTarget`. User-declared augmentations of the same interface pass through unfiltered. **Adding more entries**: each new entry needs verification against TypeScript's actual lib subsetting per target — the canonical source is `typescript-repo/src/lib/lib.esXXXX.*.d.ts` family. The 6 current entries were chosen to flip the `arrayAssignmentTest*` "29 more" → "25 more" baselines at `@target: es2015`. Other interfaces (`String`, `Number`, `Object`, `RegExp`, `Date`, etc.) may have similar pre-ES2015/post-ES2015 surface mismatches but are not yet entered. Symptom: when a SWAP candidate's diff is JUST a number difference in "and N more" / "X, Y, Z, and N more", check `LIB_MIN_TARGET` and add the missing methods.
- **Embedded `Array.map` IS generic (`map<U>(...) => U): U[]`) as of B83.4i (2026-05-28)** — but `forEach`/`find`/`flat`/`flatMap`/`keys`/`values`/`entries` are NOT. The embedded `BUILTIN_LIB_SOURCE` (Checker.kt:~23668/~23699) deliberately simplifies most Array callbacks to `=> any`/`any[]`. `map` was promoted to `map<U>(callbackfn: (value: T, index: number, array: T[]) => U): U[]` and `reduce`/`reduceRight` gained `<U>(... , initialValue: U): U` overloads so `arr.map(s => s.length)` resolves to `number[]` and `arr.reduce<string>(...)` resolves to `string`. As of B86.13 (2026-05-28) `every`/`filter` carry the real type-predicate OVERLOAD PAIR (`every<S extends T>(...): this is S[]; every(...): boolean;` and `filter<S extends T>(...): S[]; filter(...): T[];`). The element-type INFERENCE for `map` flows through `tryInferSingleTypeParamFromArgs` gate (h) (`fnTypedParamConcreteParamsBareReturnTp` — callback params all concrete after receiver T-substitution, return is the sole bare-TP `U`) + the pass-2 lambda-body-re-typing branch (Checker.kt:~54665). If you promote ANOTHER array method to generic (`flatMap`/etc.), the `any[]`→`U[]` lib change is BROAD — verify the full suite. The B83.4i inference branch handles only: concrete-callback-params + sole-bare-return-TP + un-annotated single-or-multi-param lambda + concise-or-single-return-Block body.
- **Two `implements Array` tests have CONTRADICTORY lib-snapshot baselines (Blocker #4)**: `implementArrayInterface_ts` (`MyArray<T> implements Array<T>` declaring ~25 members) expects ZERO TS2420 missing-property errors (its baseline predates `find`/`findIndex`/`fill`/`copyWithin`/`flat`/`flatMap`/`keys`/`values`/`entries` being in `Array`), while `genericArrayExtenstions_ts` (`ObservableArray<T>` declaring only `concat`) expects "length, pop, push, join, and 24 more" = 28 missing — which REQUIRES the FULL current member set. You CANNOT satisfy both by changing the embedded `Array` member set or `LIB_MIN_TARGET` filtering: dropping the 9 post-ES5 methods to flip `implementArrayInterface` regresses `genericArrayExtenstions` (its count drops to 19). The TS2420 FP on `implementArrayInterface` is therefore un-flippable surgically. B86.13 DID flip its other two FPs (the `filter` TS2416 FP via the predicate overloads; the `every` TS2416 message via the overload-aware predicate-mismatch detector in `checkClassPropertyOverrides`) — only the TS2420 remains.
- **TS2416 overload-aware predicate-mismatch (B86.13)**: `checkClassPropertyOverrides` (Checker.kt:~61078) normally `continue`s when the base member has multiple declarations (overloads), per the long-standing "skip TS2416 for overloaded base members" gotcha. EXCEPTION: when ≥1 base overload's return type is a non-asserting `this is X` TypePredicate AND the derived is a single (non-overloaded) method that is NOT itself a type predicate, it emits TS2416 with the overload-union base display `{ <S extends T>(p): this is S[]; (p): boolean; }`. This is the multi-declaration analog of B68.6's single-decl predicate-mismatch. Critically a sibling overload whose predicate return is a PLAIN type (e.g. `filter<S extends T>(...): S[]`, NOT `this is`) does NOT trigger it — only `this is`/`asserts`-free TypePredicate returns do. Helper `methodSigColonDisplayWithTypeParams` renders the `<S extends T>` prefix.
- **Call-inferred file-var TS2339 gate (B83.4i, 2026-05-28)**: `checkSinglePropertyAccess`'s file-var primitive-apparent-type branch (Checker.kt:~65116) fires TS2339 for `var n = someCall(...); n.bogus` when the call's resolved type is a concrete primitive — NOT just literal-initialized vars (the older B69.11 gate). Guarded by `currentParamBindingNames` (a checker field saved/restored at the 6 property-access-walker function-body entry sites, populated by `populateParameterLocalTypes` via `collectBindingNames` for destructured `[x]`/`{x}` params): when `identName in currentParamBindingNames`, the gate bails because the identifier refers to a destructured PARAM, not the file var. Without this guard, `function foo([x]: {a}[]){ return x.a }` + `var x = foo(...)` FP-fires TS2339 on the param `x.a` (the `localShadow` check via `currentLocalTypes` misses destructured params — `populateParameterLocalTypes` only registers Identifier params there). Any new file-var-type-driven diagnostic inside function bodies must mind this same destructured-param shadow blind spot.
- **Binder does NOT merge GetAccessor + SetAccessor into one symbol's declarations**: For `class C { get x() {...} set x(v) {...} }`, the binder creates a property symbol for `x` but its `declarations` list contains only ONE of the two accessor declarations (the first one bound). Symptom: `propSym.declarations.firstOrNull { it is SetAccessor }` returns null even when the class has a setter. **FIXED by B54.6 (2026-05-19)**: `resolveInterfaceMembers` now appends both GetAccessor and SetAccessor declarations to the same property symbol (was using `getOrPut` which kept only the first). Consumers can now `propSym.declarations.firstOrNull { it is SetAccessor }` reliably.
- **`x.x = v` write-context uses SETTER's param type, NOT getter's return type**: For accessor-pair properties, TypeScript's write-context type check uses the SetAccessor's parameter type (not the property's "main" type). Implemented by B54.5 (2026-05-19) in `checkPropertyAccessAssignment`: before resolving the property's type, look for a SetAccessor declaration on propSym and prefer its parameter type. Pairs with B54.6's accessor-pair declaration merging.
- **inferSimpleExprType deliberately skips Identifier variable-type lookup**: At Checker.kt:~59314 the helper returns null for `is Identifier -> ... else -> null` with comment "Don't look up variable types — causes FPs with enum/union targets". Multiple attempts (B54.7) to add Identifier-RHS varTypes fallback in the Identifier-target branch (`x = y` where x,y are same-base parameterized refs) initially regressed 2 tests. **Resolution (B54.9, 2026-05-19)**: combined with B54.3-narrowing (only fire when at least one type arg is a primitive — `string`, `number`, `boolean`, `bigint`, `symbol`, `void`, `null`, `undefined`, `any`, `unknown`, `never`), B54.7 is now safe to re-enable. The regression was from `class C<T> { private x: T }; C<X>` vs `C<Y>` (where X, Y are structurally identical interfaces) and `Promise<Foo>` vs `Promise<Bar>` (covariance). Both cases have named-type args (not primitive), so the narrower B54.9 gate excludes them. Same-base + primitive-arg mismatches like `A<string>` vs `A<number>` still fire correctly.
- **Strict-generic-checks for varTypes-based path (B55.x, 2026-05-19, +2 flips)**: The varTypes-based assignment check now emits TS2322 for `Foo<T>` vs `Foo<U>` (different TypeParams) via the same-base-different-TypeParam gate in `isAssignableTo`. `isAssignableTo` takes an optional `typeParams: Set<String>` param; when both args are different names in that set, returns false. emitTS2322 emits TS2208 "type parameter might need an `extends X` constraint" related info via the new `currentTypeParamDecls: Map<String, TypeParameter>` checker-instance field (populated at function-body and class-body entry). NOTE: This covers ONLY the varTypes path (function-body / method-body / class-body assignment checks). The Type-engine path's `structuredTypeRelatedTo` at Checker.kt:~55963 still returns `true` for distinct unconstrained TypeParam pairs via apparent-type compatibility — a separate piece that would require more careful verification against `infinitelyExpandingTypes4` and instantiated-Type.Reference comparisons.
- **`new C()` defaults TypeParams to `unknown` (B56.1, 2026-05-19, +1 flip)**: `getReturnTypeOfNewExpression` at Checker.kt:~44500 now instantiates `Type.Reference(C, [unknown, unknown, ...])` for `new C()` calls where C is a generic class with no explicit type args AND no constructor args to infer from. TypeParams with declared defaults use those instead of unknown. Gated on strictNullChecks. Pairs with B54.x stack: `var x = new C(); var r = x.x; x.x = r` now sees correct A<unknown> vs A<string> mismatch and emits TS2322. **Not** implemented for cases where `new C(args)` has args but inference fails — those still return un-instantiated calleeType. B56.3 (broader gate when newArgs non-empty) and B56.4 (broader when no Constructor decl) both regressed 1 test each — un-instantiated calleeType is structurally compatible with some targets in ways that C<unknown> isn't. The conservative gate is load-bearing.
- **`inferTypeArgsFromConstructorCall` is narrow** (Checker.kt:~43994): only matches when a constructor's parameter type annotation is EXACTLY a bare `TypeReference` whose name matches a TypeParam (no own typeArgs). Doesn't infer through `Array<T>`, `(x:T)=>U`, `{v:T}`, or other nested shapes. The function returns null if ANY TypeParam fails to match — there's no partial inference. Symptom: tests where `new C(arg)` should work via inference but C's constructor has `arg: SomeShape<T>` or similar nested form just fall through to the un-instantiated calleeType. Extending this is the natural next step for any "new-expression inference" work; the existing 17.31e function-arg inference (`tryInferSingleTypeParamFromArgs` at Checker.kt:~43925) is richer and could be a reference.
- **Contextual callback-param substitution needs a PARTIAL anchor mapper, not the full inference mapper (B86.1b-4, 2026-05-28, +1 flip)**: `tryInferSingleTypeParamFromArgs` returns `null` whenever ANY type param is uninferable (`if (candidates.isEmpty()) return null`). For `map<T,U>(f:(x:T)=>U, xs:T[]):U[]` called `map((a)=>a.length, [1])`, `T` anchors to `number` (from `xs:[1]`) but `U` is uninferable because the lambda body `a.length` re-types to `any`/errors — so the WHOLE mapper comes back null. The CONSUMER (B86.1b-activation's in-pass `argCtxTypes` substitution at `checkPropertyAccessInExpr`'s CallExpression branch, Checker.kt:~62769) then can't substitute `T→number` into the contextual callback param type `(x:T)=>U`, so the lambda param `a` stays a bare TypeParam and `a.length` never fires the expected TS2339. Fix: separate helper `tryInferAnchorTypeParamsForContext` (Checker.kt:~54996) gathers a PARTIAL mapper from ANCHOR positions only (bare-`T` / rest-`T[]` / non-rest `Array<T>`), returning whatever TP subset is anchorable (no all-or-nothing). Wired in as a CONSUMER fallback: `full ?: tryInferAnchorTypeParamsForContext(...)`. **Do NOT** make the full helper return a partial mapper — `getReturnTypeOfCallExpression` relies on its full-mapper-or-null contract for return-type substitution; keep the two concerns in separate helpers. Note: callback-AFTER-anchor shapes (`map<T,U>(x:T, f:(s:T)=>U)`) ALREADY work via gate (f) + the B83.4d-quick body re-typing — gate (c) at Checker.kt:~54417 was NOT the bottleneck for single-callback-param shapes.
- **TS2589 emission via depth-bail flag (B57.1, 2026-05-19, +1 flip)**: The generic-alias substitution path in `getTypeFromTypeReference` (Checker.kt:~41716) bails at `typeAliasResolutionDepth >= 10` and sets a checker-instance flag `deepInstantiationBailed`. `buildFileLocalTypeMaps` saves/resets/checks the flag around each symbol's type resolution. On bail it emits TS2589 at the relevant TypeNode's position (variable annotation OR alias body) via `emitTs2589AtTypeNode` helper that trims trailing whitespace/punctuation to land at the closing `>`. **B57.1b** gates the substitution to skip when any arg fails its TypeParam's constraint — prevents FP TS2589 on `Foo<"false", {}>` when `T extends "true"` is unsatisfied (TS2344 fires elsewhere). NOT implemented for: parameter annotations, return type annotations, expression contexts. Mapped-type recursion `{ [P in K]: N<T, K> }[K]` doesn't trigger the substitution-path recursion (uses a different code path), so tests like `recursivelyExpandingUnionNoStackoverflow_ts` still fail — extending to those is a separate piece.
- **B57.1b constraint-check gate has broader impact beyond TS2589**: The pre-recursion constraint check in `getTypeFromTypeReference`'s substitution path also prevents the recursive alias body from being evaluated when args fail constraint. This means `currentLocalTypes`/cached types for `Foo<"false", ...>` resolve to `errorType` instead of a partially-expanded structure. Downstream effects on TS2322 / TS2345 diagnostics that depend on the resolved type should be considered when extending this gate. Currently scope-bounded to the depth-bail-emit case and has zero regressions in the 10078-test suite.
- **Type.TypeParam instances partial-interning (B59.1+B59.2, 3 of 10 sites)**: At Checker.kt:~49312, `getTypeFromFunctionTypeNode`-style sites do `Type.TypeParam()` per signature resolution. This means the same source-level TypeParam (e.g. `<U>` in `function qq<U>(x: T1<U>)`) gets a NEW Type.TypeParam instance each time the function's signature is resolved (and signatures get resolved multiple times during checking — once at buildFileLocalTypeMaps init, again at each assignment-check, again at each call). Downstream caches keyed by Type id (like B58.3's substitutionResultCache) miss on subsequent calls because the resolved args have fresh ids. **B59.1+B59.2** added `typeParamInternCache: Map<Int, Type.TypeParam>` (keyed by AST position) and applied at 3 creation sites: function-signature path (49321), getTypeOfFunctionExpression (43811), symbol-typeParam resolution (49888). Other 7 sites still mint fresh. The interning is opt-in per call site — extending to all sites needs per-site verification (some sites need DISTINCT instances per call, e.g. interface call signatures where each sig has its own TypeParam set that shouldn't collide).
- **errorType displays as 'any' in typeToString (B58.1)**: `Type.Intrinsic("error")` (the errorType singleton) renders as 'any' in diagnostic messages — matches TypeScript's display convention. Other Type.Intrinsic instances (anyType, stringType, etc.) still render via `intrinsicName`. Affects any diagnostic that displays types containing errorType after substitution failure (e.g. recursive aliases that hit depth bail mid-substitution).
- **B57.3c TS2615 partner walker for mapped-type circular reference (round 50 iter3)**: `getTypeFromMappedType` captures `mappedTypeCircularInfo = (firstKey, "{ [P in \"K\"]: any; }")` at the OUTERMOST mapped-type level when depth-bail fires inside its body resolution. Gate: `isOutermost = (mappedTypeResolutionDepth == 0 on entry) && deepInstantiationBailed && !savedBailAtEntry && mappedTypeCircularInfo == null`. The `!savedBailAtEntry` check is load-bearing — without it, an outermost mapped-type whose body completes cleanly but is reached AFTER a sibling bail would mis-attribute TS2615 to itself. Consumers in `buildFileLocalTypeMaps` save/restore the info alongside `deepInstantiationBailed`, and pair `emitTs2615AtTypeNode` with `emitTs2589AtTypeNode` at the same span when info is present. Test: `recursivelyExpandingUnionNoStackoverflow_ts`.
- **Tuple-aware elaboration chain (B58.2)**: When source and target are both tuple types (Type.Object with `tupleElementTypes`) with the same arity, `getPropertyElaborationChain` emits `"Type at position N in source is not compatible with type at position N in target."` instead of the generic `"Types of property 'N' are incompatible."` used for plain objects. Matches TypeScript's tuple-mismatch chain convention. Iterates positionally over `tupleElementTypes` and short-circuits on first mismatch.
- **Recursive-alias OUTER type isn't always in aliasDisplayMap**: For `function qq<U>(x: T1<U>)` where `T1<T> = [number, T1<{x:T}>]` (recursive alias), the OUTER substitution DOES register an entry, but `typeToString` is later called with a DIFFERENT Type.Object id (verified via debug). Trace shows registration happens for ids 96, 93, 90, ... down through the recursion stack, but the type instance that `typeToString` receives in the assignment-check diagnostic has id 99 — a fresh tuple created by a subsequent re-resolution. B58.3 added `substitutionResultCache` to intern by `(symbol.id, args-id-fingerprint)`, but the cache misses on subsequent calls because the RESOLVED ARGS have different ids per call too (TypeParam(U) gets a different id each invocation — Checker.kt:~49312 creates a fresh `Type.TypeParam()` per function signature resolution). B58.4 attempted structural-id lookup but failed because element ids differ recursively. The actual fix needs either: (a) intern TypeParams by their symbol identity at Checker.kt:~49312 (so U always has the same id across function-signature resolutions), (b) recursive structural equality with cycle break in typeToString lookup, or (c) registering an `Type → (name, args)` map per assignment-check call. Direction (a) is the smallest scope fix but risks regressing many tests that rely on fresh TypeParam instances; needs careful sandboxing. Out of scope as a quick fix.

### TS2454/TS2564 gotchas

- **`any` type skips checking**: Variables/properties typed as `any` skip TS2454/TS2564.
- **`var` declarations**: TypeScript DOES check `var` for TS2454 (when strict) — only `any`-typed vars are skipped.
- **`ExportAssignment` is a use site**: `export = Foo` must be checked in `checkUsesOfUninitialized`.
- **Abstract classes still need TS2564**: Only `declare` classes are exempt, NOT `abstract`.
- **TS7030 guard**: Requires `strictNullChecks || noImplicitReturns`. TS2355 fires regardless.
- **TS2366 requires strictNullChecks**: TS2366 ("Function lacks ending return statement and return type does not include 'undefined'") fires ONLY under `strictNullChecks`. Without it, use TS7030 ("Not all code paths return a value"). Do NOT gate TS2366 on `noImplicitReturns` alone.
- **TS2355 for `undefined` in unions**: TS2355 fires for `function f(): undefined | T {}` (where T is non-void) when there are no return statements — `undefined` in a UNION does NOT satisfy "must return a value", only as a BARE `undefined` keyword (or `Promise<undefined>` for async) does. The classification in `checkBodyForImplicitReturn` (Checker.kt): `KeywordTypeNode(undefined)` and `TypeReference(Promise<KeywordTypeNode(undefined)>)` for async → "pure-undefined" (suppress all checks); UnionType-containing-undefined or `Promise<UnionType>` → "nullable" (TS2355 fires when no returns; TS7030 falls through when mixed returns).
- **`NumericLiteralNode` in method names**: All method-name extraction functions must handle it, not just `Identifier` and `StringLiteralNode`.
- **Bare specifier TS2882**: Always emit for bare (non-relative) specifiers except in AMD/System/UMD modules.

### TS1210 class strict mode gotchas

- **TS1210 vs TS1100**: TS1210 fires for `arguments`/`eval` in class bodies (always strict). TS1100 fires in external strict mode contexts (functions, modules). TypeScript NEVER emits both for the same node — TS1210 takes priority in class bodies. Suppress TS1100 inside class bodies for these names.
- **`emitDeclarationOnly` still needs checker**: Multi-file compilation with `emitDeclarationOnly` must still parse/bind/check files for diagnostics like TS1210. But use `declarationOnly = true` to limit checks — running the full checker produces FPs like TS6131 that TypeScript's declaration-only mode suppresses.
- **`isAlwaysTruthyExpr` vs `isAlwaysTruthyForOrExpr`**: In `||` contexts, TypeScript flags object-like expressions (function, arrow, object, array, class, regex) and non-empty string literals. Numeric literals and `new` expressions are NOT flagged in `||` but ARE flagged in `if`/`else if` conditions.

### Kotlin idioms

- **`*/` inside KDoc terminates the comment**: A `/** ... */` doc comment ends at the first `*/`. Embedding `*/` (e.g. when documenting a JSDoc pattern) silently breaks the rest of the declaration — a data-class body following a broken doc comment surfaces as a cascade of confusing errors like "Modifier 'override' is not applicable to 'local variable'", "No parameter with name 'pos' found", "Unresolved reference 'jsDocTagEnd'". Reword to "comment-close" or escape as `*\/`.
- **Kotlin block comments NEST — a literal `/**` *inside* a KDoc opens a nested comment level (B151)**: writing the JSDoc string `/** @overload ... */` inside a `/** ... */` doc comment makes the inner `/**` open a NESTED block comment, so the doc comment's closing `*/` only drops back to depth 1 and the comment runs to EOF → `Syntax error: Unclosed comment` at the last line + a cascade of "Unresolved reference" errors for class members BEFORE the doc comment (the whole class fails to parse). This is DISTINCT from the `*/`-closes-early gotcha above: here it's the `/**` opener that bites. When documenting JSDoc tag syntax in a KDoc, never write a literal `/**` (or `/*`) — describe it as "a JSDoc comment" or use single-line `//` comments.
- **No non-stdlib dependencies in `commonMain`**: The project targets Kotlin Native (in addition to JVM/JS), so `commonMain` must use only `kotlin.*` and `kotlinx.*` packages. No `java.*`, no `BigDecimal`, no JVM-only types. Use Kotlin's built-in numeric types and stdlib math (`kotlin.math.*`).
- **Enum context resolution** (Kotlin 2.1+): When the expected type is an enum, use unqualified entry names — write `Equals`, not `SyntaxKind.Equals`. This applies to `when` branch conditions, named arguments (`operator = Equals`), comparisons (`flags == VarKeyword`), and any other position where the enum type is inferred. Caveat: if a data class has the same name as an enum entry (e.g. `LabeledStatement`), keep the `SyntaxKind.` prefix to avoid ambiguity.
- **`in 0..<x` range checks**: Prefer `pos in 0..<end` over `pos >= 0 && end > pos` for range validation — uses Kotlin's `rangeUntil` (`..<`) operator for exclusive upper bound.
- **No JVM-only APIs in `commonMain`**: `Map.putIfAbsent` → use `getOrPut`; `Math.pow` → use `kotlin.math.pow` extension. Always use Kotlin stdlib equivalents for multiplatform compatibility.
- **`when` guard conditions** (Kotlin 2.1+): Use `when (val ch = x) { '/' if condition -> ... }` instead of `when { ch == '/' && condition -> ... }`. The `if` guard after the match value keeps pattern matching readable and avoids nested `when`/`if` blocks.

## AI agent mission

**Phase 16: Fundamental Type System Features.** Pipeline: Scanner → Parser → **Binder → Checker → Transformer → Emitter**. Phase 16 builds core type system features: contextual typing, structural comparison, overload resolution, control flow narrowing. Live test count is in `STATUS.md` (kept separate to avoid churn in this file). See `PLAN-PHASE-4.md` § "Known architectural blockers" for recurring multi-test issues that won't yield to surgical fixes.

### Execution protocol

PLAN-PHASE-4.md contains the **live QUEUE** under the heading `## Phase 16 — Fundamental Type System Features` → `### QUEUE — prioritized by unblocking potential, then by implementation cost`. (Earlier `### QUEUE` sections in the file are archived from prior phases — do not work them.) Live session notes also live under that heading, with the most recent at the top. Default order is top-to-bottom, **fixing as many items per session as the budget allows** — do not stop after a single item if there is remaining context and more tractable work ahead. The outer loop:

1. Pick the first unchecked (`- [ ]`) item in the live queue (or next unfinished sub-step of an `IN PROGRESS` item). If the top item appears blocked on missing infrastructure, **do NOT skip it** — instead, promote the unblocker to the top of the queue and work that (see autonomous-decision policy below). The original item stays unchecked and gets picked up automatically once the unblocker lands. Skipping past a blocker is reserved for the narrow user-policy cases listed under "Guardrails."
2. Implement it — the item describes the deliverable.
3. Run the full suite (`rm -rf build/test-results/jvmTest/binary && ./gradlew jvmTest 2>&1 | grep -a "tests completed"`).
4. Verify no regressions from the currently passing test count.
5. Check off the item (`- [x]`), **bump the test count in STATUS.md** to reflect the new passing total, add a session note to PLAN-PHASE-4.md (under the live notes heading, most recent on top), add a CLAUDE.md gotcha if applicable, **commit and push** (one commit per sub-step — keeps history bisectable and lets the next agent pick up mid-stream without re-running everything). STATUS.md drift is a real failure mode — past sessions committed `(+N)` work without bumping the count, so the next agent saw a stale baseline.
6. **Loop back to step 1** and pick up the next item. Keep going until one of these stop conditions:
   - Context budget is running out — finish the current item cleanly, commit, then stop.
   - Every remaining queue item is gated on user-policy decisions (Guardrails) AND no in-scope unblocker work remains. This should be rare — under the promote-unblocker default, blockers turn into queue items, so the queue rarely runs dry.
7. End the session with a concise summary of items completed, unblockers promoted (with what they unblock), items left pending user decisions, and net test count delta.

**Autonomous-decision policy (when an item appears blocked):**

When an item can't be implemented surgically — e.g. the diagnostic relies on infrastructure that doesn't exist yet (super-keyword resolution, full flow-graph, generic argument inference) — **promote the unblocker, do not skip the item**:

- **Promote-unblocker (default)**: identify the smallest concrete infrastructure piece that would unblock the item, insert it at the TOP of the queue with a one-line description and a back-pointer to the original item (and any other items it would also unblock — list them). Then start work on the unblocker. The original item stays unchecked; it gets picked up automatically on a future loop. Cross-phase work (binder + checker together, scope-chain restructuring, new cache layers) is in scope — that is exactly the work this policy exists to drive.
- **Decompose first if large**: if the unblocker is itself a multi-step change, split it into the smallest standalone sub-step that lands as a single commit without regressions, queue that, and only that. Do not attempt the whole infrastructure piece in one pass. Subsequent sub-steps get queued as separate items as the work progresses.
- **Time budget per attempt**: cap each attempt at one full-suite verification cycle. If it regresses, revert. After revert, you may either (a) try a different decomposition for the same unblocker, or (b) move to the next queue item — but record both attempts in the session note. Do not iterate more than twice in one session on the same regressing approach; if neither works, write up what you learned (which paths broke, what the underlying coupling is) and queue a follow-up "investigate X" item.
- **Skip is reserved for Guardrails only**: the only legitimate skip is when the unblocker requires a user-level decision listed under Guardrails below. For those, leave a `BLOCKED-PENDING-USER:` marker on the item with a one-paragraph proposal for the user to react to, then continue with the next queue item. Do NOT end the session.
- **No silent abandonment**: every promote/decompose/skip writes a session note (PLAN-PHASE-4.md, most recent on top) with root cause, what was attempted, and what landed. Never leave an item half-done in the working tree.

**Anti-loop rule — recon-only sessions are a protocol failure:**

A "recon-only session" is one that runs `find_candidates.py --fresh`, gets `0/0/0` (or similarly empty), spot-checks a handful of candidates, confirms they are all architectural, commits a `chore(status): refresh ... empty pool` note, and ends without landing any code change. **This is not a legitimate session outcome when the queue contains unchecked Blocker items.**

- **The `0/0/0` "exhausted" reading is almost always FALSE (fixed 2026-05-30).** The plain `find_candidates.py` EXTRA/MISSING/SWAP buckets only scan tests that ALREADY emit a parseable `error TSxxxx` line — historically ~33 of >1000 failures. The other ~70% (tests where we emit NOTHING, plus pure JS/decl/sourcemap output diffs) were structurally invisible, which is what manufactured the recurring "pool exhausted" illusion across ~20 rounds. The tool now has a **`--none`** bucket (baseline expects diagnostics, we emit none — recovered by reading the `*.errors.txt` baseline, grouped by code, fewest-error-lines-first = most tractable) and an **`--output`** bucket. **The bounded NONE tail IS the live surgical pool** (TS2307 module-resolution, TS2403, TS2367, TS2540, TS2554, TS2688, TS2344, TS2305, TS2551/2552, decl-emit TS4023/4025 …). See PLAN-PHASE-4.md § "STRATEGIC MAP of the remaining failures" for the current breakdown.
- **Hard rule**: the pool is "exhausted" ONLY when `find_candidates.py --fresh` (EXTRA/MISSING/SWAP) **and** `find_candidates.py --none --fresh` (the bounded-code NONE tail) **and** `find_candidates.py --output --fresh` are ALL dry. If any has fresh bounded candidates, work them — do NOT jump to an architectural blocker or commit a recon note. Only when all three are genuinely dry AND the queue has an unchecked `- [ ]` Blocker substep do you start that substep in the same session.
- **Diagnostic signal**: before starting a session, run `git log --oneline -10`. If three or more of the last 10 commits match `chore(status): refresh ... empty pool` (or equivalent recon-only commits), the queue is mis-structured — the agent in earlier sessions failed to promote a blocker to a checkbox. **Your first action is to fix the queue**: open PLAN-PHASE-4.md's "Known architectural blockers" section, pick the highest-yield blocker that has no corresponding `- [ ]` queue item, decompose it into the smallest standalone substep, insert it at the top of the QUEUE, commit that restructure (`chore(queue): promote Blocker #N to queue item`), and only THEN start work on it.
- **Recon is allowed as part of step 1**, not as a session deliverable. If a recon turns up surgical candidates, fine — work them. If it doesn't, that's the trigger to attack the next Blocker substep, not to wrap up.
- **Forbidden commit message patterns** when the queue has unchecked Blocker items: `chore(status): refresh post-N.N recon`, `... empty surgical pool`, `... N+ consecutive empty pool`. These are signals that the protocol has failed.
